verses.1:1: And Moab rebelled against Israel after Ahab died.
verses.1:2: And Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper chamber in Samaria and became ill; and he sent messengers and said to them, "Go and inquire of Baal the fly, god of Ekron, whether I will live from this illness of mine." And they went to inquire through him.
verses.1:3: And an angel of the Lord called Elijah the Tishbite, saying, "Rise, go to meet the messengers of Ahaziah king of Samaria, and you shall speak to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal the fly, god of Ekron? And it is not so;
verses.1:4: for thus says the Lord: "The bed onto which you went up there, you will not come down from it, for you will certainly die."'" And Elijah went and spoke to them.
verses.1:5: And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, "Why is it that you have returned?"
verses.1:6: And they said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go, return to the king who sent you, and speak to him, "Thus says the Lord: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal the fly, god of Ekron? Not so! The bed onto which you went up, surely you will not come down from it, for you will certainly die."'"
verses.1:7: And he spoke to them, "What was the manner of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
verses.1:8: And they said to him, "A hairy man, wearing a leather belt around his waist." And he said, "This is Elijah the Tishbite."
verses.1:9: And he sent to him a commander of fifty and his fifty, and he went up to him; and look, Elijah was sitting on the top of the mountain. And the commander of fifty spoke to him and said, "Man of God, the king has called you; come down."
verses.1:10: And Elijah answered and said to the commander of fifty, "And if I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty." And fire came down from heaven and devoured him and his fifty.
verses.1:11: And the king again sent to him another commander of fifty and his fifty; and the commander of fifty spoke to him and said, "Man of God, thus says the king: 'Come down quickly.'"
verses.1:12: And Elijah answered and spoke to him and said, "If I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty." And fire came down from heaven and devoured him and his fifty.
verses.1:13: And the king proceeded yet again to send a leader and his fifty; and the third commander of fifty came and bowed on his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him and spoke to him and said, "Man of God, let my life and the life of these servants of yours be precious in your eyes;
verses.1:14: look, fire came down from heaven and devoured the first two commanders of fifty; and now, please let my life be precious in your eyes."
verses.1:15: And an angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah and said, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of them." And Elijah rose and went down with him to the king.
verses.1:16: And Elijah spoke to him and said, "Thus says the Lord: 'Why is it that you sent to inquire of Baal the fly, god of Ekron? Not so! The bed onto which you went up there, you will not come down from it, for you will certainly die.'"
verses.1:17: And he died according to the word of the Lord that Elijah spoke.
verses.1:18: And the rest of the deeds of Ahaziah that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days for the kings of Israel? And Joram son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria twelve years, in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. And he did what was evil before the Lord, yet not like his brothers nor like his mother; and he sent away the pillars of Baal that his father had made and shattered them; yet he clung to the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin; he did not turn away from them. And the Lord became angry with wrath against the house of Ahab.
verses.2:1: And it happened when the Lord was bringing Elijah up in a whirlwind as into heaven, that Elijah and Elisha went from Jericho.
verses.2:2: And Elijah said to Elisha, "Now, please stay here, because God has sent me as far as Bethel." And Elisha said, "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." And he came to Bethel.
verses.2:3: And the sons of the prophets who were in Bethel came to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that the Lord is taking your master today from over your head?" And he said, "I also know; be silent."
verses.2:4: And Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, because the Lord has sent me to Jericho." And he said, "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not abandon you." And they came to Jericho.
verses.2:5: And the sons of the prophets who were in Jericho approached Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the Lord is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "Yes, I also know; be silent."
verses.2:6: And Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, because the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan." And Elisha said, "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not abandon you." And both of them went on.
verses.2:7: And fifty men, sons of the prophets, stood opposite at a distance; and both of them stood by the Jordan.
verses.2:8: And Elijah took his sheepskin and rolled it up and struck the water, and the water was divided this way and that; and both of them crossed over on barren ground.
verses.2:9: And it happened when they had crossed over that Elijah said to Elisha, "What shall I do for you before I am taken up from you?" And Elisha said, "Please let double in your spirit be upon me."
verses.2:10: And Elijah said, "You have asked something hard; if you see me being taken up from you, it will be so; and if not, it will certainly not happen."
verses.2:11: And it happened as they were going along, they walked on and talked; and look, a chariot of fire and a horse of fire, and it separated between both of them; and Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind as into heaven.
verses.2:12: And Elisha was watching, and he kept crying out, "Father, father, the chariot of Israel and its horseman!" And he saw him no longer; and he took hold of his garments and tore them into two torn pieces.
verses.2:13: And he lifted up the sheepskin of Elijah that had fallen from upon Elisha; and he stood on the bank of the Jordan.
verses.2:14: And he took the sheepskin of Elijah that had fallen from upon him, and struck the water and said, "Where is the God of Elijah, aphpho?" And he struck the waters, and they split apart this way and that; and Elisha crossed over.
verses.2:15: And the sons of the prophets and those in Jericho saw him from opposite and said, "The spirit of Elijah has rested upon Elisha." And they came to meet him and bowed down to him to the ground.
verses.2:16: And they said to him, "Look now, with your servants there are fifty men, sons of strength; please let them go and search for your master, in case the Spirit of the Lord has found him and cast him into the Jordan, or onto one of the mountains, or onto one of the hills." And Elisha said, "You shall not send."
verses.2:17: And they urged him strongly until he was ashamed, and he said, "Send." And they sent fifty men, and they searched three days, and did not find him.
verses.2:18: And he was staying in Jericho; and Elisha said, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"
verses.2:19: And the men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, the habitation of the city is good, as the master sees, but the waters are bad and the land is becoming childless."
verses.2:20: And Elisha said, "Bring me a new water jar and put salt there." And they brought it to him.
verses.2:21: And Elisha went out to the outlet of the waters, and threw salt there and said, "Thus says the Lord: 'I have healed these waters; there will no longer be from there death or childlessness.'"
verses.2:22: And the waters were healed until this day, according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.
verses.2:23: And he went up from there to Bethel; and as he was going up on the road, small boys came out from the city and mocked him and said to him, "Go up, baldhead, go up!"
verses.2:24: And he turned behind them and saw them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. And look, two bears came out from the forest and tore apart forty-two boys from among them.
verses.2:25: And he went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
verses.3:1: And Joram son of Ahab became king in Israel in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
verses.3:2: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, yet not like his father and not like his mother, and he removed the pillars of Baal that his father had made;
verses.3:3: yet he clung to the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not turn away from it.
verses.3:4: And Mesha king of Moab was a noketh, and he returned to the king of Israel in the rebellion one hundred thousand lambs and one hundred thousand fleecy rams.
verses.3:5: And it happened after Ahab died that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
verses.3:6: And King Joram went out on that day from Samaria and mustered Israel;
verses.3:7: and he went and sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, "The king of Moab has rebelled against me; will you go with me against Moab to war?" And he said, "I will go up; just as I am, so are you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses."
verses.3:8: And he said, "By what way shall I go up?" And he said, "The way of the wilderness of Edom."
verses.3:9: And the king of Israel and the king of Judah and the king of Edom went, and they made a circuit of a seven-day journey; and there was no water for the camp or for the livestock at their feet.
verses.3:10: And the king of Israel said, "Alas, for the Lord has called the three kings passing through, to give them into the hand of Moab!"
verses.3:11: And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, that we may inquire of the Lord from him?" And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, "Here is Elisha son of Jehoshaphat, who poured water over the hands of Elijah."
verses.3:12: And Jehoshaphat said, "He has a word." And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah and the king of Edom went down to him.
verses.3:13: And Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What is there between me and you? Go to the prophets of your father." And the king of Israel said to him, "No, for the Lord has called the three kings to hand them over into the hands of Moab."
verses.3:14: And Elisha said, "As the Lord of powers lives, before whom I have stood, were it not that I have regard for the person of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would neither look toward you nor see you;
verses.3:15: and now, get me a harpist." And it happened as the harpist was playing, that the hand of the Lord came upon him;
verses.3:16: and he said, "Thus says the Lord: 'Make this streambed pits upon pits.'
verses.3:17: For thus says the Lord: 'You will not see wind, and you will not see rain, yet this streambed will be filled with water, and you will drink, you and your herds and your livestock.
verses.3:18: And even this is a light thing in the eyes of the Lord; and I will hand Moab over into your hand.
verses.3:19: And you shall strike every fortified city, and you shall fell every good tree, and stop up all springs of water, and you shall make every good plot of land useless with stones.'"
verses.3:20: And it happened in the morning, as the offering was going up, that look, waters were coming from the way of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
verses.3:21: And all Moab heard that the kings had come up to fight them; and they cried out, from everyone wearing a belt, and said, "Alas!" And they stood on the border.
verses.3:22: And they rose early in the morning, and the sun rose upon the waters; and Moab saw opposite them the waters red like blood,
verses.3:23: and they said, "This is blood of the sword! The kings have fought, and each man has struck his neighbor; and now, to the plunder, Moab!"
verses.3:24: And they entered into the camp of Israel; and Israel rose up and struck Moab, and they fled before them. And they went on entering and striking Moab,
verses.3:25: and they tore down the cities; and on every good plot of land, each man threw his stone and filled it, and they stopped up every spring, and they felled every good tree, until they left the stones of the wall torn down; and the slingers surrounded and struck it.
verses.3:26: And the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, and he took with him seven hundred men with drawn swords to break through to the king of Edom; but they could not.
verses.3:27: And he took his firstborn son, who reigned in his place, and offered him up as a burnt offering upon the wall; and great remorse came upon Israel. And they departed from him and returned to the land.
verses.4:1: Now a certain woman from the sons of the prophets was crying out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant, my husband, has died, and you know that he was a servant who feared the Lord; and the creditor has come to take my two sons for himself as slaves."
verses.4:2: And Elisha said, "What shall I do for you? What do you have in the house?" And she said, "Your servant has nothing except oil with which I will anoint myself."
verses.4:3: And he said to her, "Go, ask for vessels for yourself from outside, from all the neighbors, empty vessels; do not ask for just a few.
verses.4:4: And you shall go in and shut the door behind you and behind your sons, and you shall pour out into these vessels; and what is filled you shall take away."
verses.4:5: And she went away from him and shut the door behind herself and behind her sons; they were bringing them near to her, and she was pouring until the vessels were filled.
verses.4:6: And she said to her sons, "Bring yet another vessel near to me." And they said to her, "There is no longer a vessel." And the oil stopped.
verses.4:7: And she came and reported to the man of God. And Elisha said, "Go and sell the oil and you shall pay your interest, and you and your sons shall live on the remaining oil."
verses.4:8: Now a day came when Elisha crossed over to Shunem, and a great woman was there, and she pressed him to eat bread. And it happened that as often as he went in, he turned aside to eat there.
verses.4:9: And the woman said to her husband, "Look now, I know that this is a holy man of God who passes by us continually.
verses.4:10: Let us now make for him an upper room, a small place, and let us place for him there a bed and a table and a stool and a lampstand; and it will be, when he comes in to us, that he will turn aside there."
verses.4:11: And a day came when he entered there, and he turned aside into the upper room and lay down there.
verses.4:12: And he said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman for me." And he called her, and she stood before him.
verses.4:13: And he said to him, "Say now to her, 'Look, you have put out for us all the possession; what must be done for you? Is there a word for you to the king or to the commander of the army?'" And she said, "In the midst of the people I am dwelling."
verses.4:14: And he said, "What must be done for her?" And Gehazi his servant said, "Indeed, she has no son, and her husband is an old man."
verses.4:15: And he called her, and she stood by the door.
verses.4:16: And Elisha said to her, "At this time, as the season lives, you will be embracing a son." And she said, "No, my lord, do not deceive your servant."
verses.4:17: And the woman conceived and bore a son at this time, as the season lives, as Elisha had spoken to her.
verses.4:18: And the boy grew up. And it happened, when he went out to his father, to the reapers,
verses.4:19: that he said to his father, "My head, my head!" And he said to the servant, "Carry him to his mother."
verses.4:20: And he lay upon her knees until noon, and he died.
verses.4:21: And she carried him up and laid him down upon the bed of the man of God, and she shut him in and went out.
verses.4:22: And she called her husband and said, "Send now to me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, and I will run to the man of God and return."
verses.4:23: And he said, "Why is it that you are going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath." And she said, "Peace."
verses.4:24: And she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on, go; do not hold back my riding, for if I say to you,
verses.4:25: 'Go,' then you shall go, and you shall come to the man of God at Mount Carmel." And it happened, when Elisha saw her coming, that he said to Gehazi his servant, "Look now, there is that Shunammite woman.
verses.4:26: Now run to meet her and say, 'Is it peace with you? Is it peace with your husband? Is it peace with the boy?'" And she said, "Peace."
verses.4:27: And she came to Elisha at the mountain and took hold of his feet. And Gehazi came near to push her away. And Elisha said, "Leave her alone, for her soul is deeply grieved within her, and the Lord has hidden it from me and you and has not told me."
verses.4:28: And she said, "Did I ask for a son from my lord? For did I not say, 'You shall not deal deceitfully with me'?"
verses.4:29: And Elisha said to Gehazi, "Gird your waist and take my staff in your hand and go. For if you find a man, you shall not bless him; and if a man blesses you, you shall not answer him. And you shall place my staff upon the face of the boy."
verses.4:30: And the mother of the boy said, "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will certainly not leave you." And Elisha rose up and went after her.
verses.4:31: And Gehazi passed on ahead of her and placed the staff upon the face of the boy, and there was no voice and there was no hearing. And he returned to meet him and reported to him, saying, "The boy has not awakened."
verses.4:32: And Elisha entered into the house, and look, the boy was dead, laid upon his bed.
verses.4:33: And Elisha entered into the house and shut the door behind the two of them, and he prayed to the Lord.
verses.4:34: And he went up and lay down upon the boy, and he put his mouth upon his mouth and his eyes upon his eyes and his hands upon his hands, and he bent down over him; and the flesh of the boy grew warm.
verses.4:35: And he turned back and walked in the house this way and that, and he went up and bent down over the boy up to seven times; and the boy opened his eyes.
verses.4:36: And Elisha called out to Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite woman." And he called, and she came in to him. And Elisha said, "Take your son."
verses.4:37: And the woman came in and fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground, and she took her son and went out.
verses.4:38: Now Elisha returned to Gilgal, and the famine was in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. And Elisha said to his servant, "Set on the pot, and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."
verses.4:39: And he went out into the field to gather arioth, and he found a vine in the field, and he gathered from it wild gourds, his garment full, and threw them into the pot of stew, for they did not know. And he poured out for the men to eat.
verses.4:40: And it happened, as they were eating from the stew, that look, they cried out and said, "Death is in the pot, man of God!" And they were not able to eat.
verses.4:41: And he said, "Take flour and throw it into the pot." And Elisha said to Gehazi the servant, "Pour out for the people, and let them eat." And there was no longer any bad thing there in the pot.
verses.4:42: Now a man passed through from Beth-sarisa and brought to the man of God twenty barley loaves of firstfruits and fig cakes. And he said, "Give to the people, and let them eat."
verses.4:43: And his attendant said, "What? Shall I set this before one hundred men?" And he said, "Give to the people, and let them eat, for thus says the Lord, 'They shall eat and leave some over.'"
verses.4:44: And they ate and left some over, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.5:1: Now Naaman, the commander of the army of Syria, was a great man before his master and admired in person, for by him the Lord had given deliverance to Syria; and the man was mighty in strength, a leper.
verses.5:2: And Syria went out lightly armed and took captive from the land of Israel a little girl, and she was before the wife of Naaman.
verses.5:3: And she said to her mistress, "If only my master were before the prophet of God who is in Samaria, then he would cure him from his leprosy."
verses.5:4: And she went in and reported to her lord and said, "Thus and thus spoke the girl who is from the land of Israel."
verses.5:5: And the king of Syria said to Naaman, "Go, enter, and I will send out a letter to the king of Israel." And he went and took in his hand ten talents of silver and six thousand gold pieces and ten changes of robes.
verses.5:6: And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, "And now, when this letter comes to you, look, I have sent to you Naaman my servant, and you shall cure him from his leprosy."
verses.5:7: And it happened, when the king of Israel read the letter, that he tore his garments and said, "Am I God, to put to death and to make alive, that this man sends to me to cure a man from his leprosy? For only know now and see that this man is seeking a pretext against me."
verses.5:8: And it happened, when Elisha heard that the king of Israel had torn his own garments, that he sent to the king of Israel, saying, "Why have you torn your garments? Let Naaman now come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel."
verses.5:9: And Naaman came with horse and chariot, and he stood at the door of the house of Elisha.
verses.5:10: And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go, wash yourself seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh shall return to you, and you shall be cleansed."
verses.5:11: And Naaman became angry and went away and said, "Look, I said, 'He will surely come out to me and call upon the name of his God, and place his hand upon the place, and cure the leprous spot.'
verses.5:12: Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not go and wash myself in them and be cleansed?" And he turned aside and went away in anger.
verses.5:13: And his servants came near and spoke to him, "Had the prophet spoken a great word to you, would you not do it? And how much more when he said to you, 'Wash yourself and be cleansed'!"
verses.5:14: And Naaman went down and immersed himself in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of Elisha; and his flesh returned like the flesh of a little boy, and he was cleansed.
verses.5:15: And he returned to Elisha, he and all his company, and he came and stood and said, "Look, I have come to know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel; and now, take the blessing from your servant."
verses.5:16: And Elisha said, "As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will certainly not take it." And he urged him strongly to take it, and he refused.
verses.5:17: And Naaman said, "And if not, let there now be given to your servant a gomor, pairs of mules; for your servant will no longer make a burnt offering and a sacrifice to other gods, except to the Lord.
verses.5:18: In this matter may the Lord be merciful to your servant: when my master enters into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans upon my hand, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon when he bows down in the house of Rimmon, may the Lord now be merciful to your servant in this matter."
verses.5:19: And Elisha said to Naaman, "Go in peace." And he went away from him to a debratha of the land.
verses.5:20: And Gehazi the servant of Elisha said, "Look, my master has spared this Naaman the Syrian, by not taking from his hand what he has brought. As the Lord lives, I will surely run after him and take something from him."
verses.5:21: And Gehazi pursued after Naaman. And Naaman saw him running after him, and he turned back from the chariot to meet him.
verses.5:22: And he said, "Peace. My master has sent me, saying, 'Look, just now two young men have come to me from Mount Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets; give now to them a talent of silver and two changes of robes.'"
verses.5:23: And Naaman said, "Take two talents of silver." And he took it in two bags, and two changes of robes, and he placed them upon two of his servants, and they carried them before him.
verses.5:24: And they came to the dark place, and he took them from their hands and stored them away in a house, and he sent the men away.
verses.5:25: And he himself went in and stood beside his master. And Elisha said to him, "From where, Gehazi?" And Gehazi said, "Your servant has not gone here and there."
verses.5:26: And Elisha said to him, "Did not my heart go with you when the man turned back from the chariot to meet you? And now you have taken the silver, and now you have taken the garments and olive groves and vineyards and sheep and oxen and male servants and female servants;
verses.5:27: and the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your offspring forever." And he went out from his presence leprous like snow.
verses.6:1: And the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "Look now, the place in which we live before you is too narrow for us.
verses.6:2: Let us go now as far as the Jordan, and let us take from there each man one beam, and let us build for ourselves there to live there." And he said, "Go."
verses.6:3: And one said, "Please, come with your servants." And he said, "I will go."
verses.6:4: And he went with them, and they came to the Jordan and were cutting the trees.
verses.6:5: And look, as one was felling the beam, the iron fell off into the water; and he cried out, "Oh, master! And it is hidden!"
verses.6:6: And the man of God said, "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place; and he broke off a piece of wood and threw it there, and the iron floated.
verses.6:7: And he said, "Lift it up for yourself." And he stretched out his hand and took it.
verses.6:8: And the king of Syria was waging war against Israel, and he took counsel with his servants, saying, "At such and such a place, Elimoni, I will encamp."
verses.6:9: And Elisha sent to the king of Israel, saying, "Be on your guard not to pass through this place, for Syria is hidden there."
verses.6:10: And the king of Israel sent to the place of which Elisha had told him, and he was on his guard from there not once nor twice.
verses.6:11: And the soul of the king of Syria was agitated concerning this matter, and he called his servants and said to them, "Will you not tell me who is betraying me to the king of Israel?"
verses.6:12: And one of his servants said, "No, my lord the king, for Elisha the prophet who is in Israel tells the king of Israel all the words that you speak in the inner chamber of your bedroom."
verses.6:13: And he said, "Go, see where he is, and I will send and seize him." And they told him, saying, "Look, he is in Dothan."
verses.6:14: And he sent there horses and chariots and a heavy force, and they came by night and surrounded the city.
verses.6:15: And the attendant of Elisha woke early to get up and went out, and look, a force was surrounding the city, and horses and chariots; and the young man said to him, "Oh, master! What shall we do?"
verses.6:16: And Elisha said, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."
verses.6:17: And Elisha prayed and said, "Lord, open the eyes of the young man, and let him see." And the Lord opened his eyes, and he saw; and look, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
verses.6:18: And they came down to him; and he prayed to the Lord and said, "Please strike this nation with blindness." And He struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
verses.6:19: And Elisha said to them, "This is not the city, nor is this the way; come after me, and I will lead you to the man whom you are seeking." And he led them away to Samaria.
verses.6:20: And it happened, when they entered into Samaria, that Elisha said, "Please open, Lord, their eyes, and let them see." And He opened their eyes, and they saw; and look, they were in the middle of Samaria.
verses.6:21: And the king of Israel said, when he saw them, "Shall I surely strike, father?"
verses.6:22: And he said, "You shall not strike, unless you yourself strike those whom you took captive with your sword and your bow; set loaves of bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink, and let them depart to their master."
verses.6:23: And he set before them a great feast, and they ate and drank; and he sent them away to their master. And raiding troops of Syria no longer continued to come into the land of Israel.
verses.6:24: And it happened after these things that Son of Hader, king of Syria, gathered all his army and went up, and they besieged Samaria.
verses.6:25: And there was a great famine in Samaria, and look, they were besieging it until a donkey's head came to be fifty pieces of silver, and a quarter of a kab of doves' dung, five pieces of silver.
verses.6:26: And the king of Israel was passing along upon the wall, and a woman cried out to him, saying, "Save me, lord king!"
verses.6:27: And he said to her, "May the Lord not save you! From where shall I save you? Surely not from a threshing floor or from a winepress?"
verses.6:28: And the king said to her, "What is the matter with you?" And the woman said, "This woman said to me, 'Give your son, and we will eat him today; and my son, we will eat him tomorrow.'
verses.6:29: And we boiled my son and ate him, and I said to her on the second day, 'Give your son, and let us eat him.' And she hid her son."
verses.6:30: And it happened, when the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his garments; and he was passing along upon the wall, and the people saw the sackcloth on his flesh underneath.
verses.6:31: And he said, "May God do so to me, and so may He add, if the head of Elisha remains on him today."
verses.6:32: And Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him; and he sent a man ahead of him. Before the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, "Did you know that the son of the murderer has sent to take off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and press him back at the door. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"
verses.6:33: While he was still speaking with them, look, a messenger came down to him and said, "Look, this evil is from the Lord; why should I wait for the Lord any longer?"
verses.7:1: And Elisha said, "Hear the word of the Lord: Thus says the Lord, 'About this hour tomorrow, a measure of fine flour for a shekel in the gates of Samaria.'"
verses.7:2: And the officer on whose hand the king was leaning answered Elisha and said, "Look, the Lord will make floodgates in heaven; could this thing happen?" And Elisha said, "Look, you will see it with your eyes, and from there you will not eat."
verses.7:3: And there were four leprous men beside the entrance of the city, and one man said to his neighbor, "Why are we sitting here until we die?
verses.7:4: If we say, 'Let us enter into the city,' then the famine is in the city, and we will die there; and if we sit here, then we will die. And now come, and let us throw ourselves into the camp of Syria; if they keep us alive, then we will live; and if they put us to death, then we will die."
verses.7:5: And they rose in the darkness to enter into the camp of Syria; and they came into the middle of the camp of Syria, and look, there was not a man there.
verses.7:6: And the Lord made the camp of Syria hear a sound of chariots and a sound of horses, a sound of a great force; and one man said to his brother, "Now the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us."
verses.7:7: And they rose and ran away in the darkness; and they abandoned their tents and their horses and their donkeys in the camp as it was, and fled for their lives.
verses.7:8: And these leprous men entered as far as a part of the camp, and they entered into one tent and ate and drank, and carried off from there silver and gold and clothing; and they went and returned from there and entered into another tent, and took from there and went and hid it.
verses.7:9: And one man said to his neighbor, "We are not doing thus; this day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent; and we are waiting until the light of morning, and we will find lawlessness. And now come, and let us go in and report to the house of the king."
verses.7:10: And they went in and cried out toward the gate of the city, and reported to them, saying, "We entered into the camp of Syria, and look, there is not a man there nor the voice of a person, only tied horses and donkeys, and their tents as they are."
verses.7:11: And the gatekeepers cried out and reported to the house of the king inside.
verses.7:12: And the king rose by night and said to his servants, "I will tell you now what Syria has done to us: they know that we are hungry, and they have gone out from the camp and hidden themselves in the field, saying, 'They will come out of the city, and we will seize them alive and enter into the city.'"
verses.7:13: And one of his servants answered and said, "Let them take now five of the remaining horses that were left here; look, they are like all the multitude of Israel that is perishing; and we will send there and see."
verses.7:14: And they took two riders of horses, and the king of Israel sent them after the king of Syria, saying, "Go and see."
verses.7:15: And they went after them as far as the Jordan, and look, the whole road was full of garments and equipment that Syria had thrown away in their terror; and the messengers returned and reported to the king.
verses.7:16: And the people went out and plundered the camp of Syria; and a measure of fine flour was for a shekel, according to the word of the Lord, and two measures of barley for a shekel.
verses.7:17: And the king appointed the officer, on whom the king was leaning with his hand, over the gate, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had spoken, who spoke when the messenger came down to him.
verses.7:18: And it happened just as Elisha had spoken to the king, saying, "Two measures of barley for a shekel and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, and it will be about this hour tomorrow in the gate of Samaria."
verses.7:19: And the officer answered Elisha and said, "Look, the Lord is making floodgates in heaven; this thing will certainly not happen." And Elisha said, "Look, you will see it with your eyes, and from there you will certainly not eat."
verses.7:20: And it happened so, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.
verses.8:1: Now Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, "Rise and go, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you may sojourn, for the Lord has called a famine on the land, and indeed it has come on the land for seven years."
verses.8:2: And the woman rose and did according to the word of Elisha, and she went, she and her household, and sojourned in the land of the foreigners for seven years.
verses.8:3: And it happened after the end of the seven years that the woman returned from the land of the foreigners to the city, and she came to cry out to the king concerning her house and concerning her fields.
verses.8:4: And the king was speaking to Gehazi, the attendant of Elisha the man of God, saying, "Please recount to me all the great things that Elisha has done."
verses.8:5: And it happened while he was relating to the king how he had restored a dead son to life, that look, the woman whose son Elisha had restored to life was crying out to the king concerning her house and concerning her fields. And Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life."
verses.8:6: And the king questioned the woman, and she recounted it to him. And the king gave her one eunuch, saying, "Restore all her produce of the field, from the day she left the land until now."
verses.8:7: Now Elisha came to Damascus, and Son of Hader, king of Syria, became ill. And they reported to him, saying, "The man of God has come as far as here."
verses.8:8: And the king said to Hazael, "Take a present in your hand, and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the Lord through him, saying, 'Will I live through this illness of mine?'"
verses.8:9: And Hazael went to meet him, and he took a present in his hand and all the good things of Damascus, a load of forty camels, gifts. And he came and stood before him and said to Elisha, "Your son, Son of Hader, king of Syria, has sent me to you to inquire, saying, 'Will I live through this illness of mine?'"
verses.8:10: And Elisha said, "Go, say, 'You will surely live'; and the Lord has shown me that you will surely die."
verses.8:11: And he stood before his face and set it to the point of shame, and the man of God wept.
verses.8:12: And Hazael said, "Why is it that my lord is weeping?" And he said, "Because I know all the evil things you will do to the sons of Israel: you will send their strongholds up in fire, and you will kill their chosen men with the sword, and you will smash their infants, and you will rip open their pregnant women."
verses.8:13: And Hazael said, "Who is your servant, the dead dog, that he should do this thing?" And Elisha said, "The Lord has shown me you reigning over Israel."
verses.8:14: And he departed from Elisha and went in to his master. And he said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" And he said, "He said to me, 'You will surely live.'"
verses.8:15: And it happened on the next day that he took the coverlet and dipped it in the water and wrapped it over his face, and he died. And Hazael became king in his place.
verses.8:16: In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, and of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, Joram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, became king.
verses.8:17: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem.
verses.8:18: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what was evil before the Lord.
verses.8:19: Yet the Lord was not willing to destroy Judah for the sake of David His servant, just as He had spoken to give him a lamp all the days.
verses.8:20: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and they set a king over themselves.
verses.8:21: And Joram went up to Seior, and all the chariots with him. And it happened when he rose that he struck Edom, who had surrounded him, and the commanders of the chariots; and the people fled to their tents.
verses.8:22: And Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah until this day. Then Senna revolted at that time.
verses.8:23: And the rest of the deeds of Joram and all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.8:24: And Joram slept with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father. And Ahaziah his son became king in his place.
verses.8:25: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Joram became king.
verses.8:26: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Israel. And his mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri, king of Israel.
verses.8:27: And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and he did what was evil before the Lord, just as the house of Ahab did.
verses.8:28: And he went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael, king of the foreigners, at Ramoth-gilead; and the Syrians struck Joram.
verses.8:29: And King Joram returned to be healed in Israel from the wounds with which they had struck him at Ramoth when he fought against Hazael, king of Syria. And Ahaziah son of Joram went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Israel, because he was ill.
verses.9:1: Now Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Gird your waist, and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.9:2: And you will go in there, and you will see there Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi; and you will go in and make him rise from the midst of his brothers, and bring him into the room within a room.
verses.9:3: And you will take the flask of oil and pour it on his head, and say, 'Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you as king over Israel.' And you will open the door, and flee, and not wait."
verses.9:4: And the prophet, the young man, went to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.9:5: And he went in, and look, the commanders of the army were sitting there. And he said, "I have a word for you, commander." And Jehu said, "For which one of all of us?" And he said, "For you, commander."
verses.9:6: And he rose and went into the house, and he poured the oil on his head and said to him, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: 'I have anointed you as king over the people of the Lord, over Israel.
verses.9:7: And you will destroy the house of Ahab your master from before your face, and you will avenge the blood of My servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the Lord from the hand of Jezebel
verses.9:8: and from the hand of all the house of Ahab; and you will destroy from the house of Ahab every one who urinates against a wall, both confined and abandoned in Israel.
verses.9:9: And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
verses.9:10: And the dogs will devour Jezebel in the portion of Israel, and there is no one to bury her.'" And he opened the door and fled.
verses.9:11: And Jehu went out to the servants of his master, and they said to him, "Is it peace? Why is it that this madman came in to you?" And he said to them, "You yourselves know the man and his chatter."
verses.9:12: And he said, "False! Please tell us." And Jehu said to them, "Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying," and he said, "Thus says the Lord: 'I have anointed you as king over Israel.'"
verses.9:13: And when they heard, they hurried, and each one took his garment and they placed them under him on the top of the steps, and they blew the horn and said, "Jehu has become king!"
verses.9:14: And Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram himself was keeping guard at Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael, king of Syria.
verses.9:15: And King Joram had returned to be healed in Israel from the wounds with which the Syrians had struck him when they fought against Hazael, king of Syria. And Jehu said, "If your soul is with me, let no fugitive go out from the city to go and report in Israel."
verses.9:16: And Jehu rode and went, and he went down to Israel, because Joram king of Israel was being treated in Israel from the arrow wounds with which the Arameans had shot him at Ramoth in the war against Hazael, king of Syria, for he was mighty and a man of strength. And Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.
verses.9:17: And the watchman went up onto the tower of Israel, and he saw the dust of Jehu as he was approaching, and he said, "I see dust." And Joram said, "Take a rider and send him before them, and let him say, 'Is it peace?'"
verses.9:18: And a rider on a horse went to meet them and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said, "What do you have to do with peace? Turn behind me." And the watchman reported, saying, "The messenger came up to them and has not returned."
verses.9:19: And he sent a second rider on a horse, and he came to him and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said, "What do you have to do with peace? Turn behind me."
verses.9:20: And the watchman reported, saying, "He came up to them and has not returned; and the driver was driving Jehu son of Nimshi, for he was in madness."
verses.9:21: And Joram said, "Hitch up!" And he hitched up a chariot. And Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each man in his chariot, and they went out to meet Jehu, and they found him in the portion of Naboth the Israelite.
verses.9:22: And it happened when Joram saw Jehu that he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" And Jehu said, "What peace? There are still the prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries."
verses.9:23: And Joram turned his hands and fled, and he said to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
verses.9:24: And Jehu filled his hand with the bow and struck Joram between his arms, and his arrow went out through his heart, and he sank down on his knees.
verses.9:25: And he said to Bidkar his officer, "Throw him into the portion of the field of Naboth the Israelite; for I remember, when you and I were riding in pairs behind Ahab his father, that the Lord took up this pronouncement against him:
verses.9:26: 'Surely I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday,' says the Lord, 'and I will repay him in this portion,' says the Lord. And now, please lift him up and throw him into the portion, according to the word of the Lord."
verses.9:27: And Ahaziah king of Judah saw it, and he fled by the way of Bethan. And Jehu pursued after him and said, "Him also!" And he struck him by the chariot at the ascent of Gai, which is Ekblaam. And he fled to Megiddo, and he died there.
verses.9:28: And his servants placed him on the chariot and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his tomb in the city of David.
verses.9:29: And in the eleventh year of Joram, king of Israel, Ahaziah became king over Judah.
verses.9:30: And Jehu came to Israel, and Jezebel heard, and she painted her eyes and adorned her head, and looked out through the window.
verses.9:31: And Jehu was entering the city, and she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?"
verses.9:32: And he lifted up his face to the window and saw her, and he said, "Who are you? Come down with me!" And two eunuchs looked down at him.
verses.9:33: And he said, "Roll her down!" And they rolled her down, and some of her blood splattered against the wall and against the horses, and they trampled her.
verses.9:34: And he went in and ate and drank, and he said, "Please attend to this cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."
verses.9:35: And they went to bury her, and they found nothing of her except the skull and the feet and the palms of the hands.
verses.9:36: And they returned and reported to him, and he said, "This is the word of the Lord which He spoke by the hand of Elijah the Tishbite, saying, 'In the portion of Israel the dogs will devour the flesh of Jezebel,
verses.9:37: and the carcass of Jezebel will be like dung on the face of the field in the portion of Israel, so that they will not say, "Jezebel."'"
verses.10:1: Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote a letter and sent it to Samaria, to the rulers of Samaria, and to the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab, saying,
verses.10:2: "And now, as soon as this letter comes to you, since with you are the sons of your master, and with you are the chariot and horses and fortified cities and the weapons,
verses.10:3: look for the good and the upright one among the sons of your master, and set him on the throne of his father, and fight for the house of your master."
verses.10:4: And they feared greatly and said, "Look, the two kings did not stand before him, and how will we stand?"
verses.10:5: And those who were over the house and those who were over the city and the elders and the guardians sent to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants, and whatever you say to us we will do; we will not make any man king; we will do what is good in your eyes."
verses.10:6: And he wrote to them a second letter, saying, "If you are for me and you listen to my voice, take the head of the men, the sons of your master, and bring it to me about this time tomorrow to Israel." Now the sons of the king were seventy men; these prominent men of the city were raising them.
verses.10:7: And it came about, when the letter came to them, that they took the sons of the king and slaughtered them, seventy men; and they placed their heads in baskets and sent them to him to Israel.
verses.10:8: And the messenger came and reported, saying, "I have brought the heads of the sons of the king." And he said, "Put them in two heaps beside the doorway of the gate of the city until morning."
verses.10:9: And it came about in the morning that he went out and stood, and he said to all the people, "You are righteous; look, I am the one who conspired against my master and killed him, and who struck down all these?
verses.10:10: See, appho, that nothing from the word of the Lord will fall to the ground which the Lord spoke concerning the house of Ahab; and the Lord has done all that He spoke by the hand of His servant Elijah."
verses.10:11: And Jehu struck down all those who were left in the house of Ahab in Israel, and all his prominent men and his acquaintances and his priests, so as not to leave them a remnant.
verses.10:12: And he rose and went to Samaria. He was at Beth-eked of the shepherds on the way,
verses.10:13: and Jehu found the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, "Who are you?" And they said, "We are the brothers of Ahaziah, and we have come down for the peace of the sons of the king and the sons of the ruling lady."
verses.10:14: And he said, "Seize them alive." And they slaughtered them at Beth-eked, forty-two men; he did not leave a man of them.
verses.10:15: And he went from there and took Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him, and he blessed him; and Jehu said to him, "Is your heart upright with my heart, just as my heart is with your heart?" And Jehonadab said, "It is." And Jehu said, "And if it is, give your hand." And he gave his hand, and he brought him up to himself onto the chariot,
verses.10:16: and he said to him, "Come with me and see my zeal for the Lord." And he seated him in his chariot.
verses.10:17: And he entered Samaria, and he struck down all those who were left of Ahab in Samaria until he wiped him out, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke to Elijah.
verses.10:18: And Jehu was zealous for all the people and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.
verses.10:19: And now, all you prophets of Baal, call all his servants and his priests to me; let no man be missing, for I have a great sacrifice to Baal; everyone who is missing will not live." Now Jehu acted with deceit, in order to destroy the servants of Baal.
verses.10:20: And Jehu said, "Sanctify a sacred service to Baal." And he proclaimed it.
verses.10:21: And Jehu sent throughout all Israel, saying, "And now, all his servants and all his priests and all his prophets, let no one stay away, for I am offering a great sacrifice; whoever stays away will not live." And all the servants of Baal came, and all his priests and all his prophets; not a man was left who did not arrive. And they entered the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled mouth to mouth.
verses.10:22: And he said to the one over the house of mesthaal, "Bring out clothing for all the servants of Baal." And the vestment-keeper brought it out to them.
verses.10:23: And Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab entered the house of Baal; and he said to the servants of Baal, "Search and see if there is with you any of the servants of the Lord, but only the servants of Baal alone."
verses.10:24: And he entered to offer the sacrifices and the burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed for himself eighty men outside, and he said, "Any man who escapes from the men whom I am bringing into your hands, his life shall be for his life."
verses.10:25: And it came about, when he finished offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the guards and to the officers, "Go in and strike them down; let no man come out from among them." And they struck them down with the edge of the sword, and the guards and the officers threw them out, and they went as far as the city of the house of Baal.
verses.10:26: And they brought out the robe of Baal and burned it.
verses.10:27: And they tore down the pillars of Baal, and he struck it down into latrines until this day.
verses.10:28: And Jehu wiped out Baal from Israel.
verses.10:29: However, from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, Jehu did not turn away from before them, the golden heifers in Bethel and in Dan.
verses.10:30: And the Lord said to Jehu, "Because you have done well to do what is upright in My eyes, having done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in My heart, sons of the fourth generation will sit for you on the throne of Israel."
verses.10:31: And Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the Lord, the God of Israel, with all his heart; he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.10:32: In those days the Lord began to cut off in Israel, and Hazael struck them down even in every border of Israel,
verses.10:33: from the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, all Gilead, of the Gadite and of Reuben and of Manasseh, from Aroer, which is on the bank of the torrent Arnon, both Gilead and Bashan.
verses.10:34: Now the rest of the matters of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might, and the conspiracies that he formed, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.10:35: And Jehu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:36: And the days that Jehu reigned over Israel were twenty-eight years in Samaria.
verses.11:1: Now Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son had died, and she destroyed all the seed of the kingdom.
verses.11:2: And Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of her brother and stole him from the midst of the king's sons who were being put to death, him and his nurse, in the chamber of the beds, and she hid him from the presence of Athaliah, and he was not put to death.
verses.11:3: And he was with her in the house, hidden for six years, while Athaliah was reigning over the land.
verses.11:4: And in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of hundreds, the Chorri and the Rasin, and brought them to himself into the house of the Lord, and made with them a covenant of the Lord and put them under oath. And Jehoiada showed them the son of the king,
verses.11:5: and commanded them, saying, "This is the thing that you shall do: let a third of you enter on the Sabbath, and you shall keep the watch of the house of the king at the gateway,
verses.11:6: and a third at the gate of the ways, and a third at the gate behind the guards; and you shall keep the watch of the house.
verses.11:7: And two bands among you, everyone who goes out on the Sabbath, they shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord near the king.
verses.11:8: And surround the king all around, each man with his weapon in his hand, and whoever enters into aedoth shall die." And he was with the king when he went out and when he came in.
verses.11:9: And the commanders of hundreds did all that Jehoiada the discerning commanded; and each man took his men and those entering on the Sabbath, and came in to Jehoiada the priest.
verses.11:10: And the priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears and the threefold things of King David that were in the house of the Lord.
verses.11:11: And the guards stood, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right shoulder of the house to the left shoulder of the house, along the altar and the house, all around the king.
verses.11:12: And he sent out the son of the king, and put upon him iezer and the testimony, and made him king and anointed him; and he took hold with his hand and said, "May the king live!"
verses.11:13: And Athaliah heard the sound of the runners of the people, and she went in to the people, into the house of the Lord.
verses.11:14: And she saw, and look, the king was standing by the pillar according to the ordinance, and the singers and the trumpets were beside the king, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing with trumpets. And Athaliah tore her garments and cried out, "Conspiracy! Conspiracy!"
verses.11:15: And Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds, the overseers of the army, and said to them, "Bring them out from inside the aseroth, and whoever enters after her shall surely be put to death by the sword." For the priest had said, "And let her not die in the house of the Lord."
verses.11:16: And they laid hands on her, and they entered by the way of the entrance of the horses of the house of the king, and she died there.
verses.11:17: And Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that they should be a people for the Lord, and between the king and the people.
verses.11:18: And all the people of the land entered the house of Baal and tore it down, and his altars and his images they shattered thoroughly; and they killed Magthan the priest of Baal before the altars. And the priest set overseers in the house of the Lord.
verses.11:19: And he took the commanders of hundreds, and the Chorri, and the Rassim, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the Lord; and he entered by the way of the gate of the guards of the house of the king, and they seated him on the throne of the kings.
verses.11:20: And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and they had put Athaliah to death with the sword in the house of the king.
verses.12:1: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.
verses.12:2: In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Abia, from the land of Beersheba.
verses.12:3: And Joash did what was right before the Lord all the days in which Jehoiada the priest enlightened him.
verses.12:4: However, the high places were not removed, and there the people still sacrificed and were burning incense on the high places.
verses.12:5: And Joash said to the priests, "All the silver of the holy things that is brought into the house of the Lord, silver of assessment, each man taking silver of assessment, all silver that may take hold upon a man's heart to bring into the house of the Lord,
verses.12:6: let the priests take for themselves, each man from his sale, and they themselves shall secure the breach of the house, for everything wherever a breach is found there."
verses.12:7: And it happened in the twenty-third year of King Joash that the priests had not reinforced the breach of the house.
verses.12:8: And King Joash called Jehoiada the priest and the priests, and said to them, "Why is it that you were not reinforcing the breach of the house? And now, do not take silver from your sales, for you shall give it for the breach of the house."
verses.12:9: And the priests agreed not to take silver from the people and not to strengthen the abomination of the house.
verses.12:10: And Jehoiada the priest took one chest, and bored a hole in its hole, and placed it beside Iameibin in the house of a man, the house of the Lord; and the priests who guarded the threshold gave all the silver that was found in the house of the Lord.
verses.12:11: And it happened, when he saw that there was much silver in the chest, that the scribe of the king and the high priest went up, and they bound up and counted the silver that was found in the house of the Lord.
verses.12:12: And he gave the silver that had been prepared into the hands of those doing the work, the overseers of the house of the Lord; and they paid it out to the craftsmen of wood and to the builders who were working in the house of the Lord,
verses.12:13: and to the wall-builders and to the cutters of stone, to acquire wood and cut stones to secure the breach of the house of the Lord, for everything that was spent on the house to reinforce it.
verses.12:14: However, there shall not be made for the house of the Lord silver doors, nails, bowls, and trumpets, or any gold vessel or silver vessel, from the silver that was brought into the house of the Lord;
verses.12:15: for they shall give it to those doing the work. And they reinforced the house of the Lord with it.
verses.12:16: And they did not take an account from the men into whose hands they were giving the silver to give to those doing the work, because they act in their faithfulness.
verses.12:17: Silver for sin and silver for trespass, whatever was brought into the house of the Lord, belonged to the priests.
verses.12:18: Then Hazael king of Syria went up and fought against Gath, and captured it. And Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
verses.12:19: And Joash king of Judah took all the holy things that Jehoshaphat and Joram and Ahaziah, his fathers and kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own holy things, and all the gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the house of the king, and sent them to Hazael king of Syria; and he went up from Jerusalem.
verses.12:20: And the rest of the matters of Joash, and all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.12:21: And his servants rose up and bound every conspiracy, and they struck Joash in the house of Maalo, Gaalla.
verses.12:22: And Jezichar son of Jemuath and Jezebuth, his son Shomer, his servants, struck him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David; and Amaziah his son became king in his place.
verses.13:1: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king in Samaria for seventeen years.
verses.13:2: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, and walked after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not turn away from it.
verses.13:3: And the Lord became angry in wrath against Israel, and gave them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria and into the hand of Son of Hader, son of Hazael, all the days.
verses.13:4: And Jehoahaz implored the face of the Lord, and the Lord listened to him, because He saw the oppression of Israel, because the king of Syria oppressed them.
verses.13:5: And the Lord gave deliverance to Israel, and it came out from under the hand of Syria; and the sons of Israel dwelt in their tents just as yesterday and the day before.
verses.13:6: However, they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin; in it he walked, and even the grove stood in Samaria.
verses.13:7: For there was not left to Jehoahaz a people except fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers, because the king of Syria had destroyed them, and they made them like dust for trampling.
verses.13:8: And the rest of the matters of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his mighty deeds, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:9: And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Joash his son became king.
verses.13:10: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Joash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria for sixteen years.
verses.13:11: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not turn away from all the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; in it he walked.
verses.13:12: And the rest of the matters of Joash, and all that he did, and his mighty deeds that he did with Amaziah king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:13: And Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat with his fathers and in Samaria with the brothers of Israel.
verses.13:14: And Elisha fell sick with his illness from which he died; and Joash king of Israel went down to him and wept over his face and said, "Father, father, the chariot of Israel and its horseman!"
verses.13:15: And Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." And he took a bow and arrows to him.
verses.13:16: And he said to the king, "Set your hand upon the bow." And Joash set his hand on it, and Elisha laid his hands upon the hands of the king,
verses.13:17: and said, "Open the window toward the east." And he opened it. And he said, "Arrow of deliverance for the Lord, and arrow of deliverance in Syria; and it will strike Syria in Aphek to a complete end."
verses.13:18: And Elisha said to him, "Take bows." And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground." And the king struck three times and stopped.
verses.13:19: And the man of God was grieved at him and said, "If you had struck five or six times, then you would have struck Syria to a complete end; and now you will strike Syria three times."
verses.13:20: And Elisha died, and they buried him. And raiders of Moab came into the land when the year came.
verses.13:21: And it happened, as they were burying the man, that look, they saw the raider, and they threw the man into the tomb of Elisha; and he went and touched the bones of Elisha, and he came to life and stood up on his feet.
verses.13:22: And Hazael oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
verses.13:23: And the Lord showed mercy to them and had compassion on them, and looked upon them because of His covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and the Lord was not willing to destroy them, and He did not cast them away from His presence.
verses.13:24: And Hazael king of Syria died, and Son of Hader his son became king in his place.
verses.13:25: And Joash son of Jehoahaz returned and took the cities from the hand of Son of Hader, son of Hazael, which he had taken from the hand of Jehoahaz his father in the war. Three times Joash struck him, and he restored the cities of Israel.
verses.14:1: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, became king.
verses.14:2: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Jehoaddin, from Jerusalem.
verses.14:3: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, yet not like David his father; he did according to all that Joash his father did.
verses.14:4: However, he did not remove the high places; the people still sacrificed and were burning incense on the high places.
verses.14:5: And it happened, when the kingdom became strong in his hand, that he struck down his servants who had struck down his father.
verses.14:6: And he did not put to death the sons of those who struck him down, just as it is written in the book of the laws of Moses, as the Lord commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not die for sons, and sons shall not die for fathers, but only in his own sins shall one die."
verses.14:7: He himself struck down ten thousand of Edom in Remele, and he captured the rock in the war and called its name Kathoel, until this day.
verses.14:8: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us see one another face to face."
verses.14:9: And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thistle that is in Lebanon sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And the wild beasts of the field that were in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
verses.14:10: You have indeed struck down Idumea, and your heart has lifted you up. Be glorified while staying in your house. And why do you contend in your evil? And you will fall, you and Judah with you."
verses.14:11: And Amaziah did not listen; and the king of Israel went up, and they saw one another face to face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, the land of Judah.
verses.14:12: And Judah was defeated before Israel, and each man fled to his tent.
verses.14:13: And Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah son of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh; and he came to Jerusalem and tore down four hundred cubits in the wall of Jerusalem, at the Gate of Ephraim up to the Corner Gate.
verses.14:14: And he took the gold and the silver and all the vessels found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house, and the sons of the comminglings, and he returned to Samaria.
verses.14:15: And the rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did in his might, what he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.14:16: And Joash slept with his fathers, and he was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son became king in his place.
verses.14:17: And Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
verses.14:18: And the rest of the acts of Amaziah and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.14:19: And they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; and he sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
verses.14:20: And they carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.
verses.14:21: And all the people of Judah took Azariah, and he was sixteen years old, and he became king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.14:22: He himself built Elath and restored it to Judah after the king slept with his fathers.
verses.14:23: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash reigned over Israel in Samaria forty-one years.
verses.14:24: And he did what was evil before the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.14:25: He himself removed the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the Lord, God of Israel, which He spoke by the hand of His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet who was from Gath-hepher.
verses.14:26: For the Lord saw that the affliction of Israel was very bitter, and that those who were confined, depleted, and forsaken were few, and there was no one helping Israel.
verses.14:27: And the Lord did not speak to blot out the seed of Israel from under heaven, and He saved them from the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.
verses.14:28: And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam and all that he did, and his mighty deeds, how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.14:29: And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and Azariah son of Amaziah became king in place of his father.
verses.15:1: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.
verses.15:2: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
verses.15:3: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Amaziah his father did.
verses.15:4: However, he did not remove the high places; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.15:5: And the Lord touched the king, and he was leprous until the day of his death, and he reigned in the house of Aphphusoth; and Jonathan the king's son was over the house, judging the people of the land.
verses.15:6: And the rest of the acts of Azariah and all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.15:7: And Azariah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David; and Jonathan his son became king in his place.
verses.15:8: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria six months.
verses.15:9: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, just as his fathers did; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:10: And Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, and they struck him down at Keblaam and put him to death; and he became king in his place.
verses.15:11: And the rest of the acts of Zechariah, look, they are written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:12: The word of the Lord that He spoke to Jehu, saying, "Fourth-generation sons will sit for you on the throne of Israel"; and it happened so.
verses.15:13: And Shallum son of Jabesh became king; and in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Shallum reigned for days in Samaria.
verses.15:14: And Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria, and he struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and put him to death.
verses.15:15: And the rest of the acts of Shallum and his conspiracy that he formed, look, they are written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:16: Then Menahem also struck down Tirzah and everything in it and its borders from Tirzah, because they did not open to him; and he struck it down, and he ripped open the pregnant women.
verses.15:17: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi reigned over Israel ten years in Samaria.
verses.15:18: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:19: In his days Phua king of the Assyrians went up against the land, and Menahem gave Phua one thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him.
verses.15:20: And Menahem levied the silver upon Israel, upon everyone mighty in strength, to give to the king of the Assyrians, fifty shekels for each man; and the king of the Assyrians turned back and did not remain there in the land.
verses.15:21: And the rest of the acts of Menahem and all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:22: And Menahem slept with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son became king in his place.
verses.15:23: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem reigned over Israel in Samaria two years.
verses.15:24: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:25: And Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him and struck him down in Samaria in front of the king's house, with Argob and with him Arieh; and with him were fifty men from the four hundred; and he put him to death and became king in his place.
verses.15:26: And the rest of the acts of Pekahiah and all that he did, look, they are written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:27: In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty years.
verses.15:28: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:29: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of the Assyrians came and took Ain and Abel and Thamaacha and Anioch and Kenez and Hazor and Gilead and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and he deported them to the Assyrians.
verses.15:30: And Hoshea son of Elah formed a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah, and he struck him down and put him to death, and he became king in his place in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Ahaz.
verses.15:31: And the rest of the acts of Pekah and all that he did, look, they are written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:32: In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jonathan son of Azariah king of Judah became king.
verses.15:33: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
verses.15:34: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Uzziah his father did.
verses.15:35: However, he did not remove the high places; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places. He himself built the upper gate of the house of the Lord.
verses.15:36: And the rest of the acts of Jotham and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.15:37: In those days the Lord began to send out Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah.
verses.15:38: And Jotham slept with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Ahaz his son became king in his place.
verses.16:1: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham, king of Judah, became king.
verses.16:2: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he did not do what was right in the eyes of the Lord God faithfully, like David his father.
verses.16:3: And he walked in the way of the king of Israel, and indeed he led his son through fire, and the abominations of the nations that the Lord removed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.16:4: And he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places and on the hills and under every leafy tree.
verses.16:5: Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem for war, and they laid siege against Ahaz, and they were not able to fight.
verses.16:6: At that time Rezin king of Syria restored Elath to Syria, and drove out the Judeans from Elath; and the Idumeans came to Elath and lived there to this day.
verses.16:7: And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of the Assyrians, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up, save me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me."
verses.16:8: And Ahaz took silver and gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the house of the king, and sent gifts to the king.
verses.16:9: And the king of the Assyrians listened to him; and the king of the Assyrians went up to Damascus, and captured it and deported it, and put Rezin to death.
verses.16:10: And King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet him, Tiglath-pileser king of the Assyrians, and he saw the altar in Damascus; and King Ahaz sent to Uriah the priest the likeness of the altar and its design for all its construction.
verses.16:11: And Uriah the priest built the altar according to all that King Ahaz sent from Damascus.
verses.16:12: And the king saw the altar, and went up onto it,
verses.16:13: and offered up in smoke his burnt offering and his sacrifice and his drink offering, and poured out the blood of his peace offerings upon the altar
verses.16:14: of bronze that was before the Lord; and he brought near the front of the house of the Lord from between the altar and from between the house of the Lord, and showed it on the side of the altar toward the north.
verses.16:15: And King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, saying, "Upon the great altar offer the morning burnt offering and the evening sacrifice, and the burnt offering of the king and his sacrifice, and the burnt offering of all the people and their sacrifice and their drink offering; and all the blood of a burnt offering and all the blood of a sacrifice you shall pour out upon it; upon the bronze altar it shall be for me for the morning."
verses.16:16: And Uriah the priest did according to all that King Ahaz commanded him.
