verses.16:17: And the king cut off the panels of the stands and removed the basin from them, and he took down the sea from the bronze oxen that were underneath it and put it upon a stone base.
verses.16:18: And the foundation of the seat he built in the house of the Lord, and the outer entrance of the king he turned to the house of the Lord because of the king of the Assyrians.
verses.16:19: And the rest of the acts of Ahaz, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.16:20: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David; and Hezekiah his son became king in his place.
verses.17:1: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king in Samaria over Israel for nine years.
verses.17:2: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, yet not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
verses.17:3: Against him Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians went up; and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.
verses.17:4: And the king of the Assyrians found wrongdoing in Hoshea, because he sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt and did not bring tribute to the king of the Assyrians in that year; and the king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in a prison house.
verses.17:5: And the king of the Assyrians went up in all the land, and went up to Samaria and laid siege against it for three years.
verses.17:6: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria, and deported Israel to the Assyrians, and settled them in Halah and in Habor, the rivers of Gozar, and the mountains of the Medes.
verses.17:7: And it happened because the sons of Israel sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and feared other gods,
verses.17:8: and walked in the statutes of the nations that the Lord removed from before the sons of Israel, and the kings of Israel, as many as did so,
verses.17:9: and as many of the sons of Israel as clothed themselves with words that were not so against the Lord their God; and of which they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from a tower of watchmen to a fortified city.
verses.17:10: And they set up for themselves pillars and sacred groves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
verses.17:11: And they burned incense there at all the high places, just as the nations the Lord deported from before them, and they made partners and carved, to provoke the Lord to anger.
verses.17:12: And they served the idols concerning which the Lord said to them, "You shall not do this thing to the Lord."
verses.17:13: And the Lord testified against Israel and against Judah by the hand of all His prophets, of every seer of a word: "Turn back from your evil ways, and keep My commandments and My statutes and all the law that I commanded your fathers, all that I sent to them by the hand of My servants the prophets."
verses.17:14: And they did not listen, and they hardened their back more than the back of their fathers;
verses.17:15: and His testimonies, all that He testified to them; and they walked after worthless things and became worthless, and after the nations around them, concerning which He commanded them not to do like them.
verses.17:16: They forsook the commandments of the Lord their God, and made for themselves a cast image, two heifers, and made sacred groves, and bowed down to all the host of heaven, and served Baal.
verses.17:17: And they led their sons and their daughters through fire, practiced divinations and read omens; and they sold themselves to do what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.17:18: And the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them from His presence; and none was left except the tribe of Judah all alone.
verses.17:19: And indeed Judah did not keep the commandments of God, and they walked in the statutes of Israel that they had made. And they rejected the
verses.17:20: Lord in all the offspring of Israel. And He shook them and gave them into the hand of those who plundered them, until He cast them away from His presence.
verses.17:21: For Israel was apart from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king; and Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the Lord and caused them to sin a great sin.
verses.17:22: And the sons of Israel walked in every sin of Jeroboam that he committed; they did not turn away from it
verses.17:23: until the Lord removed Israel from His presence, just as the Lord spoke by the hand of all His servants the prophets; and Israel was deported from its land to the Assyrians to this day.
verses.17:24: And the king of the Assyrians brought from Babylon, the one from Cuthah, from Avva, and from Hamath and Sepharvaim; and they were settled in the cities of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel, and they inherited Samaria and lived in its cities.
verses.17:25: And it happened at the beginning of their dwelling, they did not fear the Lord, and the Lord sent the lions among them, and they were killing among them.
verses.17:26: And they spoke to the king of the Assyrians, saying, "The nations that you deported and resettled in the cities of Samaria did not know the ordinance of the God of the land, and He sent the lions among them; and look, they are putting them to death, because they do not know the ordinance of the God of the land."
verses.17:27: And the king of the Assyrians commanded, saying, "Lead away from there, and let them go and live there, and they will instruct them in the ordinance of the land."
verses.17:28: And they brought one of the priests whom they had deported from Samaria, and he settled in Bethel, and he was instructing them how they should fear the Lord.
verses.17:29: And nation by nation they were making their own gods, and placed them in the house of the high places that the Samaritans had made, the nations in their cities in which they lived.
verses.17:30: And the men of Babylon made Rochchoth-bainithei, and the men of Cuth made Ergel, and the men of Hamath made Asimath,
verses.17:31: and the Hivites made Eblazer and Tartak and Sepharun, when they burned their sons in fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech of Sepharun.
verses.17:32: And they were fearing the Lord, and they settled their abominations in the houses of the high places that they made in Samaria, nation by nation, in the city in which they lived; and they were fearing the Lord, and they made priests of the high places, and they acted for themselves in the house of the high places.
verses.17:33: They feared the Lord, and they served their gods according to the ordinance of the nations from where he deported them.
verses.17:34: To this day they were acting according to their ordinance; they fear, and they act according to their statutes and according to their judgment, and according to the law and according to the commandment that the Lord commanded the sons of Jacob, whose name He set as Israel.
verses.17:35: And the Lord made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, "You shall not fear other gods or bow down to them, and you shall not serve them, and you shall not sacrifice to them;
verses.17:36: but rather to the Lord, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great strength and with a high arm; Him you shall fear, and to Him you shall bow down, to Him you shall sacrifice.
verses.17:37: And be careful all the days to do the statutes and the ordinances and the law and the commandments that He wrote for you, and you shall not fear other gods.
verses.17:38: And you shall not forget the covenant that He made with you; and you shall not fear other gods,
verses.17:39: but rather you shall fear the Lord your God, and He will deliver you from all your enemies;
verses.17:40: and you shall no longer listen to their ordinance that they practice."
verses.17:41: And these nations were fearing the Lord, and they were serving their carved images; and indeed the sons and the sons of their sons do just as their fathers did, to this day.
verses.18:1: And it happened in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, that Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.
verses.18:2: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Abu, daughter of Zechariah.
verses.18:3: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done.
verses.18:4: He himself removed the high places, and shattered the pillars, and destroyed the groves and the bronze serpent that Moses had made, because until those days the sons of Israel had been burning incense to it; and he called it Nesthalei.
verses.18:5: In the Lord, the God of Israel, he put his hope; and after him there was no one like him among the kings of Judah, nor among those who were before him.
verses.18:6: And he clung to the Lord; he did not turn away from following Him, and he kept His commandments, all that He had commanded Moses.
verses.18:7: And the Lord was with him, and in all that he did he acted wisely; and he rebelled against the king of the Assyrians and did not serve him.
verses.18:8: He himself struck down the foreigners as far as Gaza and as far as its border, from a tower of watchmen even to a fortified city.
verses.18:9: And it happened in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, that Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, went up against Samaria and laid siege against it.
verses.18:10: And he seized it at the end of three years, in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea, king of Israel, and Samaria was captured.
verses.18:11: And the king of the Assyrians deported Samaria to the Assyrians, and placed them in Halah and in Habor, the river of Gozan, and in Ore of the Medes,
verses.18:12: because they did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God, and they transgressed His covenant, all that Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded; and they did not listen and did not do them.
verses.18:13: And in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, went up against the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
verses.18:14: And Hezekiah, king of Judah, sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachish, saying, "I have sinned; turn back from me. Whatever you impose on me, I will bear." And the king of the Assyrians imposed on Hezekiah, king of Judah, three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
verses.18:15: And Hezekiah gave all the silver that was found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house.
verses.18:16: At that time Hezekiah cut off the doors of the temple and the supports that Hezekiah, king of Judah, had overlaid with gold, and gave them to the king of the Assyrians.
verses.18:17: And the king of the Assyrians sent Tartan, Raphis, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a heavy force against Jerusalem; and they went up and came to Jerusalem, and they stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool, which is on the road of the fuller's field.
verses.18:18: And they called out to Hezekiah, and Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward, and Shebna the scribe, and Jehoshaphat the recorder came to him.
verses.18:19: And Rabshakeh said to them, "Say now to Hezekiah, 'Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you trust?
verses.18:20: You said—only words of the lips—"Counsel and strength for war." Now then, in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?
verses.18:21: Now look, you have trusted for yourself on this crushed reed staff, on Egypt; if any man leans on it, it will go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to all who trust in him.
verses.18:22: And since you said to me, "We trust in the Lord God," did not this very Hezekiah remove His high places and His altars, and say to Judah and to Jerusalem, "Before this altar you shall worship in Jerusalem"?'
verses.18:23: And now enter into dealings with my lord, the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able to put riders on them for yourself.
verses.18:24: And how will you turn back the face of one governor among the least of my lord's servants? Yet you yourself have put your hope in Egypt for chariots and horsemen.
verses.18:25: And now, is it without the Lord that we have come up against this place to destroy it? The Lord said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"
verses.18:26: And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, and Shebna, and Joash said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Syrian; we understand it, and do not speak with us in Judean. And why are you speaking in the ears of the people who are on the wall?"
verses.18:27: And Rabshakeh said to them, "Was it to your lord and to you that my lord sent me to speak these words? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, who are to eat their own dung and drink their own urine together with you?"
verses.18:28: And Rabshakeh stood and cried out loudly in Judean, and spoke and said, "Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians.
verses.18:29: Thus says the king: 'Do not let Hezekiah mislead you with words, for he will by no means be able to deliver you from his hand,
verses.18:30: and do not let Hezekiah make you hope in the Lord, saying, "The Lord will surely deliver; this city will by no means be given into the hand of the king of the Assyrians."'
verses.18:31: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of the Assyrians: 'Make a blessing with me and come out to me, and each man will drink his own vine, and each man will eat his own fig tree, and drink water from his own cistern,
verses.18:32: until I come and take you to a land like your own land, of grain and wine and bread and vineyards, a land of oil-bearing olive trees and honey; and you will live and by no means die. And do not listen to Hezekiah, for he deceives you, saying, "The Lord will rescue you."
verses.18:33: Have the gods of the nations indeed rescued, each one his own country, from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
verses.18:34: Where is the god of Hamath and Arpad? Where is the god of Sepharvaim? And have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
verses.18:35: Who among all the gods of the lands have delivered their lands from my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?'"
verses.18:36: And they kept silent and did not answer him a word, for it was the king's command, saying, "You shall not answer him."
verses.18:37: And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward, and Shebna the scribe, and Joash son of Shaphan, the recorder, came in to Hezekiah with their garments torn, and reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.
verses.19:1: And it happened, when King Hezekiah heard it, that he tore his garments and clothed himself in sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord.
verses.19:2: And he sent Eliakim the steward and Shebna the scribe and the elders of the priests, clothed in sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
verses.19:3: And he said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: This day is a day of distress and rebuke and provocation, for children have come to birth pangs, and there is no strength in the one giving birth.
verses.19:4: Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of the Assyrians, his master, sent to reproach the living God and to blaspheme with the words that the Lord your God has heard; so take up a prayer for the remnant that is found."
verses.19:5: And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
verses.19:6: And Isaiah said to them, "This is what you will say to your master: 'This is what the Lord says: Do not be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the lads of the king of the Assyrians have blasphemed.
verses.19:7: Look, I am putting a spirit in him, and he will hear a report and return to his own land; and I will strike him down by the sword in his own land.'"
verses.19:8: And Rabshakeh returned and found the king of the Assyrians fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.
verses.19:9: And he heard concerning Thara, king of the Ethiopians, saying, "Look, he has come out to fight with you." And he returned and sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
verses.19:10: "Do not let your God, in whom you trust, elate you, saying, 'Jerusalem will by no means be handed over into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.'
verses.19:11: Look, you have heard all that the kings of the Assyrians have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction; and will you be rescued?
verses.19:12: Did the gods of the nations deliver them? Did not my fathers destroy both Gozan and Haran, and Raphis, and the sons of Eden who were in Thaesthen?
verses.19:13: Where is the king of Math and the king of Arpad? And where are Sepharvaim, Hanes, and Udu?"
verses.19:14: And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them; and he went up to the house of the Lord, and Hezekiah unfolded them before the Lord.
verses.19:15: And he said, "Lord, the God of Israel, who sits upon the cherubim, You alone are God in all the kingdoms of the earth; You made heaven and earth.
verses.19:16: Incline Your ear, Lord, and hear; open Your eyes, Lord, and see, and hear the words of Sennacherib, which he sent to reproach the living God.
verses.19:17: For in truth, Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have laid waste the nations.
verses.19:18: And they have put their gods into the fire, for they are not gods, but only works of human hands, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.
verses.19:19: And now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth will know that You alone are the Lord God."
verses.19:20: And Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "This is what the Lord, the God of powers, the God of Israel, says: What you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians, I have heard.
verses.19:21: This is the word that the Lord has spoken against him: The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and mocked you; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
verses.19:22: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? And against whom have you raised your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.19:23: By the hand of your messengers you have reproached your Lord, and you have said, 'With the multitude of my chariots I will ascend to the height of the mountains, the flanks of Lebanon; and I cut down the stature of its cedar, the choicest of its cypresses; and he came into the midst of forest and Carmel.
verses.19:24: I cooled off and drank foreign waters, and with the sole of my foot I laid waste all the rivers of siege.'
verses.19:25: I formed it, I gathered it; and it came to be for elevations from warlike dwellings, fortified cities.
verses.19:26: And those who live in them grew weak in hand; they stumbled and were put to shame; they became grass of the field or green vegetation, green shoots of the rooftops, and something trampled before one who stands.
verses.19:27: And I know your sitting down and your going out and your coming in, and your rage against Me.
verses.19:28: Because you have raged against Me, and your arrogance has come up into My ears, I will put My hooks in your nostrils and a bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back on the way by which you came.
verses.19:29: And this will be the sign for you: eat this year what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs up; and in the third year, sowing and reaping and planting of vineyards, and you will eat their fruit.
verses.19:30: And what is left will add the survivor of the house of Judah, a root below, and will produce fruit above.
verses.19:31: For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go forth, and a survivor from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord of powers will do this.
verses.19:32: Not so! This is what the Lord says concerning the king of the Assyrians: He will not enter this city, and he will not shoot an arrow there, and a shield will not go before him, and he will by no means pour out a siege mound against it.
verses.19:33: By the way that he came, by it he will return, and he will not enter this city, says the Lord.
verses.19:34: And I will shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant."
verses.19:35: And it happened at night that an angel of the Lord went out and struck down in the camp of the Assyrians one hundred eighty-five thousand; and they rose early in the morning, and look, they were all dead bodies.
verses.19:36: And Sennacherib king of the Assyrians departed and went and returned, and lived in Nineveh.
verses.19:37: And it happened, as he was worshiping in the house of Esdrach his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.
verses.20:1: In those days Hezekiah became ill to the point of death. And Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came in to him and said to him, "This is what the Lord says: Give orders to your house; you are dying and will not live."
verses.20:2: And Hezekiah turned toward the wall, and prayed to the Lord, saying,
verses.20:3: "Please, O Lord, remember now how I have walked before You in truth and with a full heart, and have done Your good in Your eyes." And Hezekiah wept with a great weeping.
verses.20:4: And Isaiah was in the middle court, and the word of the Lord came to him, saying,
verses.20:5: "Return, and you will say to Hezekiah, the leader of My people, 'This is what the Lord, the God of David your father, says: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look, I will heal you; on the third day you will go up to the house of the Lord.
verses.20:6: And I will add fifteen years to your days, and from the hand of the kings of the Assyrians I will save you and this city; and I will shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.'"
verses.20:7: And he said, "Let them take a cake of figs and put it on the boil, and he will recover."
verses.20:8: And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What is the sign that the Lord will heal me, and that I will go up to the house of the Lord on the third day?"
verses.20:9: And Isaiah said, "This is the sign from the Lord that the Lord will do the word that He has spoken: the shadow will go ten steps, if it returns ten steps."
verses.20:10: And Hezekiah said, "It is a light thing for the shadow to decline ten steps; no, rather let the shadow return on the stairway ten steps backward."
verses.20:11: And Isaiah the prophet cried out to the Lord, and the shadow returned on the stairway ten steps backward.
verses.20:12: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Balaan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been ill.
verses.20:13: And Hezekiah rejoiced over them, and he showed them the entire house of nechotha, the silver and the gold, the spices and the good oil, and the house of the vessels, and all that was found in his treasuries; there was not a thing that Hezekiah did not show them in his house and in all his dominion.
verses.20:14: And Isaiah the prophet came in to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say, and from where have they come to you?" And Hezekiah said, "From a distant land they have come to me, from Babylon."
verses.20:15: And he said, "What did they see in your house?" And he said, "All that is in my house they saw; there was nothing in my house that I did not show them, and even the things in my treasuries."
verses.20:16: And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the Lord:
verses.20:17: Look, days are coming when everything that is in your house and all that your fathers have stored up until this day will be taken to Babylon; and not a word that the Lord has spoken will be left behind.
verses.20:18: And your sons who will come forth from you, whom you will father, he will take, and they will be eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon."
verses.20:19: And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "Good is the word of the Lord that He has spoken."
verses.20:20: And the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and all that he made, the pool and the aqueduct, and brought the water into the city, are these not written in the book of the acts of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.20:21: And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and Manasseh his son became king in his place.
verses.21:1: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for fifty-five years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Hephzibah.
verses.21:2: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord removed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.21:3: And he returned and built the high places that Hezekiah his father had torn down, and he set up an altar to Baal, and made groves just as Ahab king of Israel had done, and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
verses.21:4: And he built an altar in the house of the Lord, as He had said, "In Jerusalem I will place My name."
verses.21:5: And he built an altar for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.21:6: And he led his sons through fire, and practiced divination and augury, and appointed a medium and multiplied spiritists, so as to do what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.21:7: And he placed the carved image of the grove in the house of which the Lord had spoken to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house in Jerusalem, I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, and I will place My name forever,
verses.21:8: and I will not again move the foot of Israel from the land that I gave to their fathers—those who will keep all that I commanded, according to the entire commandment that My servant Moses commanded."
verses.21:9: And they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray to do what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, more than the nations that the Lord destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.21:10: And the Lord spoke by the hand of His servants the prophets, saying,
verses.21:11: "Because Manasseh the king of Judah has done these abominations, more evil than all that the Amorite who was before did, and has even caused Judah to sin with their idols;
verses.21:12: not so; thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, 'Look, I am bringing calamities upon Jerusalem and upon Judah, so that both ears of everyone who hears will ring;
verses.21:13: and I will stretch out over Jerusalem the measure of Samaria and the plumb weight of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe out Jerusalem just as an alabaster jar is wiped out when it is wiped, and is turned over onto its face;
verses.21:14: and I will cast off the remnant of My inheritance, and I will hand them over into the hands of their enemies, and they will become plunder and spoil to all their enemies,
verses.21:15: because he did what was evil in My eyes, and they have been provoking Me to anger from the day I brought their fathers out of Egypt and until this day.'"
verses.21:16: And indeed, Manasseh shed very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem from edge to edge, besides their sins by which he caused Judah to sin, to do what was evil in the eyes of the Lord.
verses.21:17: And the rest of the deeds of Manasseh, and all that he did, and his sin that he sinned, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:18: And Manasseh slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza; and Amos his son reigned in his place.
verses.21:19: Amos was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for two years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Meshullam, daughter of Haruz from Jesebal.
verses.21:20: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, just as Manasseh his father had done.
verses.21:21: And he walked in every way in which his father had walked, and served the idols that his father had served, and bowed down to them.
verses.21:22: And he abandoned the Lord God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the Lord.
verses.21:23: And the servants of Amos conspired against him, and put him, the king, to death in his house.
verses.21:24: And the people of the land struck down all those who had conspired against King Amos; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
verses.21:25: And the rest of the deeds of Amos, all that he did, look, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:26: And they buried him in his tomb in the garden of Uzza; and Josiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:1: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for thirty-one years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Jedeia, daughter of Edeina, from Basuroth.
verses.22:2: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, and walked in every way of David his father; he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.22:3: And it happened in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, in the eighth month, that the king sent Shaphan son of Eliah, son of Meshullam, the scribe of the house of the Lord, saying,
verses.22:4: "Go up to Hilkiah the great priest and seal the silver that has been brought into the house of the Lord, which those who guard the threshold have gathered from the people,
verses.22:5: and let them give it into the hand of those doing the work, those appointed in the house of the Lord." And he gave it to those doing the work who were in the house of the Lord, to fortify the breach of the house,
verses.22:6: to the carpenters and to the builders and to the masons, and to purchase timber and quarried stones to reinforce the breach of the house.
verses.22:7: However, they did not call them to account for the silver being given to them, because they act in faithfulness.
verses.22:8: And Hilkiah the great priest said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
verses.22:9: And he went into the house of the Lord to the king, and brought back word to the king and said, "Your servants have melted down the silver that was found in the house of the Lord, and have given it into the hand of those doing the work who are appointed in the house of the Lord."
verses.22:10: And Shaphan the scribe spoke to the king, saying, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read it before the king.
verses.22:11: And it happened, when the king heard the words of the book of the law, that he tore his garments.
verses.22:12: And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Achbor son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah, servant of the king, saying,
verses.22:13: "Go and inquire of the Lord on my behalf, and on behalf of all the people, and on behalf of all Judah, and concerning the words of this book that has been found; for great is the wrath of the Lord that has been poured out upon us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of the book, to do according to all that is written against us."
verses.22:14: And Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam, and Achbor, and Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, mother of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, the keeper of the wardrobe; and she lived in Jerusalem in the Masena; and they spoke to her.
verses.22:15: And she said, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to Me,
verses.22:16: 'Thus says the Lord: Look, I am bringing calamities upon this place and upon those who dwell in it, all the words of the book that the king of Judah read,
verses.22:17: because they abandoned Me and burned incense to other gods, so that they might provoke Me to anger with the works of their hands; and My fury will be kindled in this place, and will not be quenched.'
verses.22:18: And to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the Lord, thus you shall say to him: 'Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: As for the words that you have heard,
verses.22:19: because your heart was softened and you humbled yourself before the face of the Lord when you heard all that I spoke against this place and against those who dwell in it, to become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your garments and wept before Me; indeed, I also have heard, says the Lord.
verses.22:20: Not so; look, I am adding you to your fathers, and you will be gathered into your tomb in peace, and it will not be seen by your eyes among all the calamities that I Myself am bringing upon this place.'"
verses.23:1: And the kings brought back the word; and the king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.23:2: And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and every man of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people, from small even to great; and he read before them all the words of the book of the covenant that was found in the house of the Lord.
verses.23:3: And the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord, to keep His commandments and His testimonies and His statutes with all the heart and with all the soul, to establish the words of this covenant, the things written in this book; and all the people stood in the covenant.
verses.23:4: And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest and the priests of the second order and those guarding the threshold to bring out of the temple of the Lord all the vessels that had been made for Baal and for the grove and for all the host of heaven; and he burned them outside Jerusalem in Salemoth of Kidron, and took their dust to Bethel.
verses.23:5: And he burned the chomarim whom they had given to the king of Judah, and they were burning incense on the high places and in the cities of Judah and in the places around Jerusalem, and those burning incense to Baal and to the sun and to the moon and to the mazuroth and to all the host of heaven.
verses.23:6: And he brought out the grove from the house of the Lord outside Jerusalem to the brook Kidron, and burned it in the brook Kidron and ground it fine into dust, and threw its dust into the grave of the sons of the people.
verses.23:7: And he demolished the house of the kadesim who were in the house of the Lord, where the women were weaving chettiin there for the grove.
verses.23:8: And he brought up all the priests from the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense there, from Gaibal even to Beersheba; and he demolished the house of the gates that was beside the doorway of the gate of Joshua, ruler of the gate, those on a man's left in the gate of the city.
verses.23:9: However, the priests of the high places did not go up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, but rather they ate unleavened bread in the midst of their brothers.
verses.23:10: And you will defile Topheth in the valley of the son of Hinnom, for a man to make his son pass through and a man his daughter to Molech in fire.
verses.23:11: And he burned the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun at the entrance of the house of the Lord, by the treasury of Nathan the king, the eunuch, in Pharurim; and he burned the chariot of the sun with fire.
verses.23:12: And the altars that were on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the king of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, the king demolished and pulled down from there, and threw their dust into the brook Kidron.
verses.23:13: And the house facing Jerusalem, on the right of the mountain of Mosoath, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Astarte, the detestable thing of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh, the detestable thing of Moab, and for Milcom, the abomination of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled.
verses.23:14: And he shattered the pillars and utterly destroyed the groves, and filled their places with human bones.
verses.23:15: Furthermore, the altar that was in Bethel, the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat made, who caused Israel to sin—even that altar, the high place, he pulled down, and shattered its stones and ground them fine into dust, and burned the grove.
verses.23:16: And Josiah turned aside and saw the graves there in the city, and sent and took the bones from the graves and burned them on the altar, and defiled it according to the word of the Lord that the man of God had spoken when Jeroboam stood at the feast by the altar. And turning, he lifted up his eyes to the grave of the man of God who had spoken these words.
verses.23:17: And he said, "What is that monument that I see?" And the men of the city said to him, "The man of God who came out of Judah and proclaimed these words that he proclaimed against the altar of Bethel."
verses.23:18: And he said, "Leave it alone; let no man move his bones." And his bones were rescued along with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.
verses.23:19: Moreover, all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, Josiah removed, and he did in them all the deeds that he had done in Bethel.
verses.23:20: And he sacrificed all the priests of the high places who were there upon the altars, and burned human bones upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.23:21: And the king commanded all the people, saying, "Keep the Passover to the Lord our God, as it is written in the book of this covenant."
verses.23:22: For this Passover had not been held since the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
verses.23:23: But only in the eighteenth year of King Josiah was the Passover held to the Lord in Jerusalem.
verses.23:24: Moreover, the wishers and the knowers and the teraphim and the idols and all the detestable things that were in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem Josiah cleared away, so that he might establish the words of the law that were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the Lord.
verses.23:25: Like him there was no king before him who turned to the Lord with all his heart and with all his strength and with all his soul, according to all the law of Moses, and after him no one like him arose.
verses.23:26: However, the Lord did not turn away from the great wrath of His anger with which He burned in His anger against Judah, on account of the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him to anger.
verses.23:27: And the Lord said, "I will also remove Judah from His presence, just as I removed Israel, and I will reject this city that I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name will be there.'"
verses.23:28: And the rest of the acts of Josiah and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.23:29: Now in his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of the Assyrians, to the Euphrates River, and Josiah went to meet him; and Neco put him to death at Megiddo when he saw him.
verses.23:30: And his servants carried him dead from Makedon and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his grave. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.
verses.23:31: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Hamitai, daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
verses.23:32: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.23:33: And Pharaoh Neco deposed him at Ablaa in the land of Hamath so that he would not reign in Jerusalem, and he gave one hundred talents of silver and one hundred talents of gold.
verses.23:34: And Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, king over them in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim; and he took Jehoahaz and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.
verses.23:35: And Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; however, they assessed the land to give the silver at the command of Pharaoh; each man according to his assessment, they gave the silver and the gold with the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Neco.
verses.23:36: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Iella, daughter of Edil from Kruma.
verses.23:37: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.24:1: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon went up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years; then he turned and rebelled against him.
verses.24:2: And he sent against him the raiders of the Chaldeans and the raiders of Syria and the raiders of Moab and the raiders of the sons of Ammon, and sent them out into the land of Judah to prevail, according to the word of the Lord that He spoke by the hand of His servants the prophets.
verses.24:3: However, it was because of the wrath of the Lord against Judah, to remove it from His presence for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done.
verses.24:4: And also he shed innocent blood and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the Lord was not willing to be appeased.
verses.24:5: And the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did—look, are these not written in the book of the records of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.24:6: And Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiakim his son became king in his place.
verses.24:7: And the king of Egypt did not again go out from his land, for the king of Babylon had taken, from the brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River, all that belonged to the king of Egypt.
verses.24:8: Jehoiakim was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.
verses.24:9: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that his father had done.
verses.24:10: At that time Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon went up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
verses.24:11: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon entered into the city, and his servants were besieging it.
verses.24:12: And Jehoiakim king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his servants and his mother and his officials and his eunuchs; and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.
verses.24:13: And he brought out from there all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the house of the king, and cut in pieces all the golden vessels that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the Lord, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.24:14: And he exiled Jerusalem and all the officials and the mighty in strength, capturing ten thousand captives, and every craftsman and the locksmith; and no one was left except the poor of the land.
verses.24:15: And he exiled Jehoiakim to Babylon, and the king's mother and the king's wives and his eunuchs; and the strong of the land he led away into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.24:16: And all the men of might, seven thousand, and the craftsman and the locksmith, one thousand, all of them mighty, making war—the king of Babylon brought them into deportation to Babylon.
verses.24:17: And the king of Babylon made Matthan his son king in his place, and set his name as Zedekiah.
verses.24:18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Mitat, daughter of Jeremiah.
verses.24:19: And he did what was evil before the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
verses.24:20: For it was because of the wrath of the Lord upon Jerusalem and in Judah, until He cast them away from His presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.25:1: And it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem, and encamped against it, and built a siege wall against it all around.
verses.25:2: And the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah, on the ninth day of the month.
verses.25:3: And the famine grew severe in the city, and there were no loaves of bread for the people of the land.
verses.25:4: And the city was breached, and all the men of war went out by night by the way of the gate between the walls, the one that belongs to the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were against the city all around. And he went by the way of the Arabah.
verses.25:5: And the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king and overtook him in Araboth of Jericho, and all his army was scattered away from him.
verses.25:6: And they seized the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Ierdeblatha, and he spoke judgment with him.
verses.25:7: And he slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and blinded the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him in fetters, and brought him to Babylon.
verses.25:8: And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the chief cook, standing before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.25:9: And he burned the house of the Lord, and the house of the king, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and the chief cook burned every house.
verses.25:11: And Nebuzaradan the chief cook carried away the rest of the people who were left in the city, and the defectors who had defected to the king of Babylon, and the remainder of the support.
verses.25:12: And the chief cook left behind some of the poor of the land as vinedressers and as tabein.
verses.25:13: And the Chaldeans broke in pieces the bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the mechonoth, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the Lord, and carried their bronze to Babylon.
verses.25:14: And he took the pots, and the iamein, and the bowls, and the censers, and all the bronze vessels with which they minister.
verses.25:15: And the chief cook took the firepans and the bowls, the gold ones and the silver ones.
verses.25:16: Two pillars, the one sea, and the mechonoth that Solomon made for the house of the Lord: there was no weighing of the bronze of all the vessels.
verses.25:17: Eighteen cubits was the height of the one pillar, and the bronze chothar was upon it, and the height of the chothar was three cubits; sakacharthai were upon the chothar all around, all of bronze; and in the same way for the second pillar upon the gabacha.
verses.25:18: And the chief cook took Seraiah the first priest, and Zephaniah, son of the second rank, and the three who guarded the threshold.
verses.25:19: And from the city he took one eunuch who was overseer of the fighting men, and five men of those who saw the face of the king who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
verses.25:20: And Nebuzaradan the chief cook took them and led them away to the king of Babylon at Deblatha.
verses.25:21: And the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. And Judah was carried into exile away from its land.
verses.25:22: And as for the people who were left in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon left behind, he appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.
verses.25:23: And all the commanders of the army, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah; and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Jonah son of Kareth, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Nepphathite, and Ozonias son of the Achathite, they and their men.
verses.25:24: And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and said to them, "Do not fear the passage of the Chaldeans; settle in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you."
verses.25:25: And it happened in the seventh month that Manael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the seed of the kings, came, and men with him; and he struck Gedaliah so that he died, as well as the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
verses.25:26: And all the people arose, from small even to great, and the commanders of the armies, and entered into Egypt, because they were afraid of the presence of the Chaldeans.
verses.25:27: And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiakim king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiakim king of Judah and brought him out of the house of his imprisonment.
verses.25:28: And he spoke good things with him, and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.25:29: And he changed the garments of his imprisonment, and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.
verses.25:30: And his food allowance was a continual food allowance; it was given to him from the house of the king, a day's portion in its day, all the days of his life.

notes.1:2: Greek renders the deity's name literally as "Baal the fly" (translating Hebrew zebub, "fly," and shifting from the masculine article in 1:2-3 to the feminine article in 1:6, 16), and adds the final clause "And they went to inquire through him."
notes.1:3: Greek reads "And it is not so" (and "Not so!" in 1:6, 16), reflecting Hebrew lo-ken ("not so") where the Masoretic Text reads laken ("therefore").
notes.1:7: Greek krisis (literally "judgment") renders Hebrew mishpat in the sense of "manner, bearing, or appearance."
notes.1:18: The Septuagint places Joram's accession summary here (instead of the Masoretic synchronism in 1:17), reading "his brothers" rather than "his father" (compare 3:2) and adding that he shattered Baal's pillars and that the Lord became angry against the house of Ahab.
notes.2:1: Greek reads "from Jericho" (where the Masoretic Text has "from Gilgal") and qualifies Elijah's ascent with "as into heaven" (also in 2:11).
notes.2:8: Greek melote specifically denotes a sheepskin garment (also in 2:13-14), and en eremo (literally "in a desert/barren ground") contrasts with the Masoretic Text's "on dry ground."
notes.2:13: Greek explicitly reads "from upon Elisha," whereas the Masoretic Text reads "from upon him" (referring to Elijah).
notes.2:14: Greek leaves Hebrew aph-hu ("even he") untranslated as the transliteration aphpho, and omits "the Lord" before "the God of Elijah."
notes.2:16: Greek reads "has found him" (rather than "has lifted him up") and adds "into the Jordan" before the mountains and hills.
notes.3:4: Greek transliterates Hebrew noqed ("sheep breeder") as noketh and adds "in the rebellion" (en te epanastasei).
notes.3:11: Greek distinctly names Elisha's father as "Jehoshaphat" (Iosaphath), identical to the king of Judah in the same verse, where the Masoretic Text has "Shaphat."
notes.3:21: Greek renders the mobilization phrase actively and reads "and said, 'Alas!'" where the Masoretic Text has "and upward."
notes.3:25: Where the Masoretic Text names the city Kir-hareseth, Greek translates the elements as common words: "the stones of the wall torn down."
notes.3:27: Greek reads "great remorse" (metamelos megas) rather than "great wrath" (Masoretic Text qetsep gadol).
notes.4:2: The Greek reads "oil with which I will anoint myself" (ho aleipsomai elaion), rendering the Hebrew term for a flask or jar as a verb meaning to anoint.
notes.4:13: The Greek reads "all the possession" (ten pasan enktesin), widely regarded as an early scribal variant for ekstasin ("anxiety" or "trouble," matching the Hebrew).
notes.4:35: The Greek states that Elisha bent down over the boy up to seven times before the boy opened his eyes, lacking the Hebrew statement that the boy sneezed seven times.
notes.4:39: "Arioth" is an untranslated Greek transliteration of a Hebrew plural noun referring to wild herbs or greens.
notes.4:42: The Greek reads the distinct place name Beth-sarisa (Baithsareisa, corresponding to Baal-shalishah in Hebrew) and "fig cakes" (palathas, where the Hebrew has fresh grain in a sack).
notes.5:4: The Greek has the feminine reflexive pronoun heautes ("her lord"), making Naaman's wife the one who reports to her husband rather than Naaman reporting to the Syrian king as in the Hebrew.
notes.5:17: The Greek reads "a gomor, pairs of mules" (gomor, zeuge hemionon), using the dry measure gomor (possibly a variant for gomos, "load") and omitting the Hebrew reference to earth or soil.
notes.5:19: "Debratha" is an untranslated Greek transliteration of a Hebrew term for a stretch of distance (kibrat, apparently read with d for k).
notes.5:24: The Greek reads "to the dark place" (eis to skoteinon), rendering the Hebrew word for a hill or citadel (ha-opel) as though from a similar root meaning darkness.
notes.5:26: Instead of the Hebrew question ("Is it a time to accept silver...?"), the Greek reads declarative statements ("And now you have taken the silver, and now you have taken the garments..."), reading "time" as "now" and the infinitive as a second-person verb.
notes.6:5: The Greek reads "hidden" (kekrymmenon), likely an early inner-Greek shift from kechremenon ("borrowed," matching the Hebrew).
notes.6:8: "Elimoni" is a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew indefinite term almoni ("unnamed" or "such and such"), placed alongside the translated phrase "such and such."
notes.6:24: "Son of Hader" renders the Greek huios Hader, which translates the Ben- element ("son of") and reflects a resh/dalet variant of the Hebrew name Ben-hadad.
notes.6:25: The Greek gives the price of a donkey's head as fifty pieces of silver, whereas the Hebrew reads eighty.
notes.6:27: The Greek uses a negative optative (me se sosai Kyrios, "May the Lord not save you!"), expressing a negative wish rather than a conditional clause ("If the Lord does not save you").
notes.7:1: The Greek here omits the parallel clause about two measures of barley for a shekel, which appears later in vv. 16 and 18.
notes.7:9: "We are not doing thus" literally renders the Greek ouch houtos (a calque of the Hebrew idiom for "not right"), and "we will find lawlessness" makes the speakers the subject rather than guilt finding them.
notes.7:13: The Greek presents a single comparison ("they are like all the multitude of Israel that is perishing," using eisin pros) where the Hebrew has a doubled clause.
notes.7:14: The Greek reads "two riders of horses" and "after the king of Syria," where the Hebrew reads "two chariots with horses" and "after the army of Aram."
notes.7:17: The Greek reads "the messenger" (matching 6:33), whereas the Hebrew reads "the king."
notes.8:7: The Greek text renders the Syrian king's name literally as "Son of Hader" (Hebrew Masoretic Text: "Ben-hadad"). In 8:8-9, "present" translates the Greek loanword maana (from Hebrew minchah, "gift/tribute").
notes.8:10: The Greek text reads second-person singular "you will surely die" (Hebrew Masoretic Text: "he will surely die"). In 8:11, "set it to the point of shame" literally renders the Greek expression for staring fixedly until embarrassed.
notes.8:13: The Greek text reads "the dead dog" (Hebrew: "the dog") and "reigning over Israel" (Hebrew Masoretic Text: "king over Aram/Syria"). In 8:15, "coverlet" renders the transliterated Greek loanword chabba (a woven bedcloth).
notes.8:17: The Greek text states that Joram reigned "forty years" in Jerusalem, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "eight years." In 8:21-22, the Greek place names "Seior" and "Senna" correspond to Hebrew "Zair" and "Libnah."
notes.8:28: "King of the foreigners" follows the Greek text (the same term used for the Philistines in 8:2-3), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "king of Aram/Syria." In 8:26 and 8:29, the Greek text reads "Israel" where the Hebrew reads "Jerusalem" (8:26) and "Jezreel" (8:29).
notes.9:7: The Greek text adds "from before your face" and uses second-person verbs in 9:7-8 ("you will avenge" and "you will destroy"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has first-person verbs spoken by God ("I will avenge" and "I will cut off").
notes.9:13: "Top of the steps" renders the Greek phrase containing the transliterated Hebrew loanword garem (literally "the garem of the steps"), referring to the bare landing or upper platform of the stairs.
notes.9:16: The Greek text includes a major expansion detailing Joram's arrow wounds from "the Arameans" and adding "for he was mighty and a man of strength." Throughout chapter 9 (9:10, 15-17, 21, 25, 30, 36-37), the Greek reads "Israel" and "Israelite" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Jezreel" and "Jezreelite."
notes.9:20: The Greek text literally reads "the driver was driving Jehu son of Nimshi, for he was in madness," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously."
notes.9:27: The Greek place names "Bethan," "Gai," and "which is Ekblaam" correspond to Hebrew "Beth-haggan," "Gur," and "by Ibleam." In 9:32, the Greek text also adds "and saw her," reads "Who are you? Come down with me!" (Hebrew: "Who is on my side? Who?"), and mentions "two eunuchs" (Hebrew: "two or three eunuchs").
notes.10:6: Greek reads "Israel" here and in vv. 7 and 11 (and "Samaria" in v. 1) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Jezreel." Greek also reads "these prominent men" rather than "with the great men."
notes.10:10: Greek leaves the Hebrew particle epho ("then, now") untranslated as the transliteration appho.
notes.10:18: Greek reads "was zealous for" (ezelosen) where the Hebrew text reads "gathered."
notes.10:22: Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for "wardrobe" (meltahah) as mesthaal, and renders the closing subject as "the vestment-keeper" (ho stolistes).
notes.10:26: Greek reads "the robe of Baal" (ten stolen, likely an inner-Greek shift from "pillar") rather than "the pillars of the house of Baal," and in v. 27 reads singular "struck it down into latrines" (lytronas).
notes.11:4: Greek transliterates the Hebrew military titles for "the Carites and the guards" with singular articles as "the Chorri and the Rasin" (spelled "Rassim" in v. 19).
notes.11:8: Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for "ranks" (sederoth) as aedoth here and aseroth in v. 15 (where Greek also reads plural "them" and "from inside"), and closes v. 8 with past indicative "and he was" rather than an imperative.
notes.11:10: Greek "the threefold things" (tous trissous) translates a rare Hebrew term for shields or quivers, apparently connecting it with the Hebrew root for "three"; in v. 9 Greek likewise styles Jehoiada "the discerning" (ho synetos) rather than "the priest."
notes.11:12: Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for "crown" or "diadem" (hannezer) as iezer, and reads singular "took hold with his hand" (ekratesen, likely a variant of ekrotesen, "clapped") where Hebrew has plural "they clapped their hands."
notes.11:18: Greek reads the distinct name form Magthan (an uncial variant of Mattan) where Hebrew has Mattan; earlier in v. 14 Greek reads "the singers" (hoi oidoi) where Hebrew has "the captains."
notes.12:2: Greek names Joash's mother Abia (Hebrew: Zibiah) and adds "the land of" before Beersheba.
notes.12:6: Greek reads "his sale" (and "your sales" in v. 8), interpreting Hebrew makkar as "sale" rather than "acquaintance." Here and in vv. 7-8, 13, "breach" renders the Hebrew loanword bedek ("breach/disrepair") transliterated directly in the Greek.
notes.12:9: Greek reads "the abomination (bdelygma) of the house," likely an inner-Greek scribal corruption of the transliterated bedek ("breach") appearing in vv. 6-8 and 13.
notes.12:10: Greek literally reads "in its hole" (Hebrew: "in its lid"), retains a garbled location name Iameibin (Hebrew: "the altar on the right side"), and reads "in the house of a man" (Hebrew: "as a man enters").
notes.12:17: Unlike Hebrew ("was not brought"), Greek omits the negation ("whatever was brought") and places sin silver before trespass silver.
notes.12:21: Greek literally reads "bound every bond/conspiracy" and has the distinct place names Maalo and Gaalla (Hebrew: Millo and Silla).
notes.12:22: Greek has the distinct names Jezichar, Jemuath, and Jezebuth (Hebrew: Jozacar, Shimeath, and Jehozabad), and literally reads "his son Shomer" (Hebrew: "son of Shomer").
notes.13:3: Greek renders Hebrew Ben-hadad literally as "Son of Hader" (also in vv. 24-25), with final -r reflecting a Hebrew d/r interchange.
notes.13:5: Greek reads the abstract noun "deliverance" (soteria) where Hebrew has "deliverer/savior."
notes.13:13: Greek reads "Jeroboam sat with his fathers and in Samaria with the brothers of Israel," diverging sharply from Hebrew ("Jeroboam sat on his throne; and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel").
notes.13:17: Greek omits the command "Shoot!" and its execution, and uses third-person singular "it will strike" (Hebrew: "you will strike").
notes.13:18: Greek uses plural toxa ("bows," sometimes meaning arrows) where Hebrew has "the arrows," and v. 19 reads "was grieved" where Hebrew has "was angry."
notes.14:7: The Greek renders Hebrew 'Valley of Salt' as the place name Remele, translates Hebrew Sela as 'the rock', and reads Kathoel where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Joktheel.
notes.14:13: The Greek names Amaziah's grandfather as Jehoahaz, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Ahaziah.
notes.14:14: The phrase 'the sons of the comminglings' reflects a literal Greek rendering of the Hebrew idiom for hostages, connecting the Hebrew term with a root meaning 'to mingle'.
notes.14:25: The Greek text reads 'removed' (apestesen), likely an early textual shortening of 'restored' (apekatestesen), corresponding to 'restored' in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.14:27: The Greek reads 'the seed of Israel' and 'from the hand of Jeroboam', whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'the name of Israel' and 'by the hand of Jeroboam'.
notes.14:29: The Greek text names Azariah son of Amaziah—king of Judah—as reigning in place of his father here, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text names Jeroboam's successor as Zechariah his son.
notes.15:5: The Greek reads 'reigned' for Hebrew 'lived', transliterates Hebrew 'separate house' as Aphphusoth, and names the king's son Jonathan here and in verses 7 and 32, but Jotham in verses 30, 36, and 38.
notes.15:10: The Greek treats the Hebrew phrase 'before the people' as the place name Keblaam and uses plural verbs for the assassins.
notes.15:16: The Greek reads Tirzah in both occurrences, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Tiphsah followed by Tirzah.
notes.15:19: The Greek names the Assyrian king Phua where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Pul, and omits the closing Hebrew clause about strengthening the kingdom in his hand.
notes.15:25: The Greek reads 'in front of the king's house' and 'from the four hundred', whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'in the citadel of the king's house' and 'of the Gileadites'.
notes.15:29: The Greek gives distinct place-name forms (Ain, Abel and Thamaacha as two towns, Anioch, and Kenez) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text lists Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, and Kedesh; the Greek also spells Tiglath-pileser as Algathphellasar.
notes.15:30: The Greek reads 'Jotham son of Ahaz', whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Jotham son of Uzziah'.
notes.16:3: The Greek reads singular "king of Israel" and "and the abominations" rather than "kings of Israel" and "according to the abominations" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.16:14: In the Greek, "of bronze that was before the Lord" directly modifies the altar at the end of v. 13, followed by "brought near the front of the house of the Lord" and "showed it" (edeixen, where the Hebrew has "placed it").
notes.16:15: The Greek reads "upon the bronze altar it shall be for me for the morning" (eis to proi), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew consonants as "morning" rather than "to inquire."
notes.16:17: "Stands" translates the Greek loanword mechonoth, a transliteration of the Hebrew term for the temple's wheeled bronze stands.
notes.16:18: The Greek reads "the foundation of the seat he built" and "turned to the house of the Lord," diverging from the Hebrew reference to removing the covered Sabbath structure from the house of the Lord.
notes.17:4: "Segor" is the distinct Septuagint name corresponding to "So" in the Hebrew text; "tribute" here and in v. 3 translates the Greek Semitic loanwords manaa and manach, and "wrongdoing" renders Greek adikian (vs. Hebrew "conspiracy").
notes.17:6: The Greek reads plural "rivers of Gozar" (vs. Hebrew "river of Gozan") and "the mountains of the Medes" (Ore Medon, reflecting Hebrew "mountains" rather than "cities").
notes.17:11: The Greek reads "made partners and carved" (koinonous kai echaraxan), whereas the Hebrew text has "did wicked things."
notes.17:19: The Greek splits "they rejected the Lord" across vv. 19-20, making the people the subject (followed in v. 20 by "He shook them"), whereas the Hebrew reads "the Lord rejected all the offspring of Israel and afflicted them."
notes.17:30: In vv. 30-31 the Greek preserves distinctive names—Rochchoth-bainithei, Ergel, Asimath, the Hivites (Huaioi), and Eblazer—and treats Sepharun as a third deity made by the Hivites rather than as the people who burned their children.
notes.17:34: Unlike the Hebrew text, the Greek omits the negations here ("they fear, and they act according to their statutes..."), and in v. 40 continues the Lord's command in the second person ("you shall no longer listen") rather than resuming third-person narrative.
notes.18:2: Greek reads "Abu" (Abou), whereas the Hebrew text has "Abi."
notes.18:4: Greek reads "Nesthalei" where Hebrew has "Nehushtan" (and other Greek witnesses read "Neesthan"); Greek also uses plural "the groves" for Hebrew "the Asherah."
notes.18:11: Greek reads "Samaria" where Hebrew has "Israel," and accents "Ore of the Medes" as a proper name transliterating Hebrew are ("cities of"), whereas other Greek editions accent it ore ("mountains of the Medes").
notes.18:17: Greek reads "Raphis" where Hebrew has "Rab-saris," and spells Tartan as "Thanthan."
notes.18:18: Greek names the recorder "Jehoshaphat" here and "Joash" or "Joash son of Shaphan" in verses 26 and 37, where Hebrew consistently has "Joah son of Asaph."
notes.18:31: "Make a blessing with me" translates Greek eulogian literally, reflecting a Hebrew idiom for coming to peaceful terms; Greek also reads "drink" of the vine where Hebrew has "eat."
notes.19:4: Greek reads 'and to blaspheme with the words' (parallel to 'to reproach') where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'and will rebuke the words'; in 19:3 Greek also reads singular 'he said' rather than plural, and here spells 'remnant' as lemmatos (for leimmatos).
notes.19:12: Greek divides the verse into two questions rather than one relative clause and uses the LXX-distinct names Raphis (Hebrew Rezeph) and Thaesthen (Telassar), as well as Thara (Tirhakah) in 19:9 and Math (Hamath), Hanes (Hena), and Udu (Ivvah) in 19:13, where it also omits 'the king of the city of' before Sepharvaim.
notes.19:23: Greek reads 'your Lord' (kyrion sou, MT 'the Lord') and shifts to third-person 'he came into the midst of forest and Carmel'; in 19:24 it renders 'I dug' as 'I cooled off' (epsyxa) and 'Egypt' as 'siege' (perioches).
notes.19:25: Greek lacks the opening clause ('Have you not heard? Long ago I did it...') and reads 'for elevations from warlike dwellings'; in 19:30 Greek has the unusual accusative 'will add the survivor,' and in 19:32 reads 'Not so!' (ouch houtos, for Hebrew lo ken) instead of MT 'Therefore' (laken).
notes.19:37: Greek names Sennacherib's god Esdrach, corresponding to Nisroch in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.20:3: Greek adds the possessive in 'Your good in Your eyes'; in 20:4 it states simply 'Isaiah was in the middle court' rather than Hebrew 'had not gone out of the middle court/city.'
notes.20:7: Greek omits Isaiah's name and makes the entire instruction part of his spoken command ('and put it on the boil, and he will recover') rather than narrative past action.
notes.20:9: Greek renders Hebrew im ('or' in an alternative question) literally as ean ('if'), forming a conditional statement; in 20:11 'the shadow' is the grammatical subject and the reference to the steps of Ahaz is absent.
notes.20:12: Greek reads Merodach-baladan son of Balaan (MT Berodach-baladan son of Baladan) and uses the Hebrew loanword manaan (minchah, 'gift'); in 20:13 Greek leaves the obscure Hebrew term nekhot untranslated as nechotha, likely referring to a royal storehouse or treasury.
notes.20:17: Greek adds the relative pronoun 'that' (ho), reading 'not a word that the Lord has spoken will be left behind' (MT 'nothing shall be left, says the Lord'); in 20:19 Greek reads 'He has spoken' and omits Hezekiah's following remark about peace and truth in his days.
notes.21:6: The Greek text reads "ellen," a scribal corruption in Codex Vaticanus of "theleten" ("medium" or "necromancer," cf. 23:24) preserved in other Greek witnesses. The Greek also reads plural "his sons" (Hebrew: "his son").
notes.21:12: Greek "not so" (ouch houtos) is a characteristic kaige-Septuagint rendering of Hebrew "therefore" (lakhen) read as "lo khen" ("not so"); the same rendering recurs in 22:20.
notes.21:13: The Greek reads "an alabaster jar" (ho alabastros), where the Hebrew text reads "a dish."
notes.21:16: Literally "mouth to mouth" (stoma eis stoma), a Semitic idiom meaning from one edge or end to the other. The Greek also reads plural "their sins" (Hebrew: "his sin").
notes.21:18: The Greek text names Manasseh's son "Amos" throughout vv. 18-25 (Hebrew: "Amon"), and in v. 19 calls his mother "Meshullam" from "Jesebal" (Hebrew: "Meshullemeth" from "Jotbah").
notes.22:1: The Greek text reads "Jedeia," "Edeina," and "Basuroth," where the Hebrew text reads "Jedidah," "Adaiah," and "Bozkath."
notes.22:3: The Greek adds "in the eighth month," names Shaphan's father "Eliah" (Greek Eliou; Hebrew: "Azaliah"), and calls Shaphan "the scribe of the house of the Lord" (Hebrew: "the scribe, to the house of the LORD").
notes.22:5: In v. 4 the Greek reads "seal the silver" (Hebrew: "sum up the silver"), and here shifts from Josiah's command to narrative ("And he gave it"). "Breach" renders Greek "to bedek" (also v. 6), a direct transliteration of the Hebrew term for structural damage.
notes.22:14: The Greek describes Huldah as the "mother" of Shallum (Hebrew: "wife") and transliterates her Jerusalem district as "the Masena" (Hebrew: "the Second Quarter"). The Greek manuscript here also spells Ahikam and Shaphan as "Acheikath" and "Saphphath."
notes.22:20: As in 21:12, Greek "Not so" renders Hebrew "therefore," and "adding you" reflects Greek prostithemi (Hebrew: "gathering you"). The verse ends with a passive construction ("it will not be seen") and emphatic "ego eimi epago" ("I Myself am bringing"), a hallmark of the kaige recension.
notes.23:1: The Greek text begins this verse with plural "the kings brought back the word," corresponding to the close of 22:20 in the Hebrew ("and they brought back word to the king").
notes.23:5: Greek reads "burned" (Hebrew "deposed"), singular "to the king of Judah," and retains untranslated Hebrew terms as "chomarim" (idolatrous priests) and "mazuroth" (constellations), as also with "Salemoth" (v. 4), "kadesim" and "chettiin" (v. 7), and "Pharurim" (v. 11). Throughout the chapter, "grove" translates Greek alsos (Hebrew Asherah).
notes.23:10: Greek has second-person plural future "you will defile" and omits the negation before "for a man to make his son pass through" (Hebrew "and he defiled... so that no one might make... pass through"). Nearby, Greek reads "Gaibal" for Geba and "house of the gates" (v. 8), translates Nathan-melech literally as "Nathan the king" (v. 11), and turns Hebrew "of Destruction" into the proper name "Mosoath" (v. 13).
notes.23:16: Greek reads "in the city" (Hebrew "on the mountain") and contains a longer ending describing Jeroboam standing by the altar at the feast and Josiah lifting his eyes toward the grave of the man of God.
notes.23:24: "Wishers" and "knowers" are literal Greek etymological renderings of the Hebrew terms for mediums and spiritists. In v. 27, the Greek text reads third-person "from His presence" inside the Lord's first-person speech.
notes.23:33: Greek reads "deposed him at Ablaa" (Hebrew "imprisoned him at Riblah") and "one hundred talents of gold" (Hebrew "one talent of gold"). Nearby LXX-distinct proper names are "Makedon" (v. 30, for Megiddo), "Hamitai" (v. 31, for Hamutal), and "Iella", "Edil", and "Kruma" (v. 36, for Zebudah, Pedaiah, and Rumah).
notes.24:2: Greek omits an explicit subject ("the Lord" in Hebrew) for "sent," leaving Nebuchadnezzar as the apparent grammatical subject, and reads "to prevail" (Hebrew "to destroy it").
notes.24:3: Greek reads "because of the wrath of the Lord" (Hebrew "at the command of the Lord"), matching the wording of v. 20.
notes.24:6: Here and in vv. 8, 12, and 15, the Greek text names the new king "Jehoiakim," identical to his father's name, whereas the Hebrew distinguishes the son as "Jehoiachin."
notes.24:10: Greek states that Nebuchadnezzar himself went up to Jerusalem (omitting "the servants of" found in Hebrew) and in v. 11 that he "entered into the city" (Hebrew "came against the city").
notes.24:17: Greek reads "Matthan his son" (Hebrew "Mattaniah his uncle"). In v. 18, Greek names Zedekiah's mother "Mitat" (Hebrew "Hamutal," compare "Hamitai" in 23:31) and omits "from Libnah."
notes.25:6: The Greek renders the place name as Ierdeblatha here (and Deblatha in v. 20), contrasting with Riblah in v. 21; similarly, Araboth of Jericho in v. 5 transliterates the Hebrew word for plains.
notes.25:8: Greek archimageiros literally means chief cook (rendering the Hebrew title for the captain of the guard), and standing before the king of Babylon replaces the Hebrew servant of the king of Babylon. Verse 10 (the demolition of Jerusalem's walls) is absent in this Greek text after v. 9.
notes.25:17: Several Hebrew architectural and occupational terms in vv. 12-17 are transliterated rather than translated in the Greek: tabein (v. 12, plowmen), mechonoth (vv. 13, 16, stands), iamein (v. 14, shovels), chothar (v. 17, capital), and sakacharthai and gabacha (v. 17, latticework). Similarly, v. 11 reads support (for Hebrew multitude), and v. 18 reads son of the second rank (for Hebrew second priest).
notes.25:23: Several names here and in v. 25 differ from the Hebrew Masoretic Text: Jonah son of Kareth (for Johanan son of Kareah), the Nepphathite (for the Netophathite), Ozonias son of the Achathite (for Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite), and Manael in v. 25 (for Ishmael, also omitting the number ten). In v. 24, Greek parodon (passage) reflects a variant Hebrew reading rather than servants.
notes.25:27: The Greek reads Ioakim (Jehoiakim) twice here, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Jehoiachin; the Greek also adds from the house of the king in v. 30.
